sections.title: 47-51 ON THE DAY OF JUDGMENT ALL OTHER GODS TO WHOM PEOPLE WORSHIP BESIDES ALLAH SHALL VANISH

translation.text: The knowledge of the Hour rests solely with Him. Not a fruit comes forth from its sheath, nor does any female conceive nor give birth to a child but it is in His knowledge. On that Day He will call out to them: “Where are those associates of Mine?” They will answer: “We have declared to You that none of us can bear witness to that.”

commentary.text: Do not concern yourselves regarding the timing of the Day of Resurrection as only Allah SWT is the One Who knows when it will occur, rather be concerned about the consequences of your sins and deviations on that day. Nothing is hidden from Allah SWT, therefore, no one in His kingdom should act fearlessly or with impunity. Worship Allah SWT alone and do not commit shirk.

Hadith: Once when the Prophet (PBUH) was on a journey, a man on the way shouted his name from a distance. The Prophet (PBUH) asked what he wanted to say. He said: When will Resurrection come? The Prophet (PBUH) replied: It must come, in any case! What preparations have you made for it?
Lesson: Do not get caught up in minutia that detracts from the main message and do not follow false deities. Focus on what is important!

translation.text: And if We let them taste a mercy from Us after being touched with adversity, they will certainly say, “This is what I deserve. I do not think the Hour will ˹ever˺ come. And if in fact I am returned to my Lord, the finest reward with Him will definitely be mine.” But We will surely inform the disbelievers of what they used to do. And We will certainly make them taste a harsh torment.

commentary.text: If after adversity some good/relief/mercy arrives they again revert to the rejection of Allah SWT. They ascribe false expectations with Allah SWT saying that, ‘since I am getting good in this world then I deserve and will get good in the Hereafter as well’. Thus, by receiving gifts and mercy from Allah SWT they feel they deserve it, that is, I have gotten all this because of my being worthy of it. It is my right that I should receive all this. This attitude is Kufur (disbelief).

translation.text: When We show favour to someone, they turn away, acting arrogantly. And when touched with evil, they make endless prayers ˹for good˺.

commentary.text: The nature of an infidel is being stated here that when Allah Almighty bestows upon him the good things: wealth, honor and peace, the infidel gets so involved in them and so intoxicated with them that he becomes even more distant from the true Benefactor, Allah Almighty, and his pride and heedlessness increase even more. But when he faces some distress, then he starts long and lengthy supplications to Allah Almighty. Here the Qur'an has used the word ` broad' to describe their lengthy supplications,

Lengthy supplications in themselves are praiseworthy and desirable as is proved by authentic ahadith about the etiquettes of supplication where it is mentioned that, while praying to Allah Ta’ ala, beseeching tearfully and repeatedly is desirable. (Bukhari and Muslim) Therefore, the denunciation of the infidel is actually not for lengthy supplications, but for his duplicitous disposition that when Allah blesses him with His bounties, he gets intoxicated with arrogance and pride, and when he faces distress, he keeps on praying in a way of wailing and complaining about his difficulties, as is the habit of heedless people.
Lesson: Do not be a hypocrite and ingrate because Allah SWT dislikes both traits.

sections.title: 52-54 HAVE YOU EVER CONSIDERED THAT IF AL-QURAN IS REALLY FROM ALLAH AND YOU DENY IT, WHAT WILL HAPPEN TO YOU

translation.text: Tell them, (O Prophet): “Did you ever consider: if this Quran is indeed from Allah and you still deny it, who can be in greater error than he who goes far in fiercely opposing it?”

commentary.text: This does not mean that one should believe only owing to the fear that if the Quran is truly from Allah SWT one is inviting doom by denying it. But it means this: It is not wisdom that you should be bent upon stubbornly opposing the Quran without first attempting to understand what it says.

translation.text: We will show them Our signs in the universe and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that this Quran is the truth. Is it not enough that your Lord is a Witness over all things?

commentary.text: The Quran and the Proofs of its Truth
Allah SWT tells us to reflect upon His creation and His signs.

Today we have new sciences developing that enable us to look deeper inside ourselves (physical composition) via biology, chemistry and neurology etc. Similarly, we now are able to closely observe the universe/galaxies, nature, geology etc., with renewed clarity of understanding. As this multi-faceted exploration develops one can very clearly see a parallel between the Quran and modern science and the fact that there is no incongruity or conflict within the two. In fact, it is becoming clearer that the miracle called Quran is the total and complete Truth.

translation.text: Lo, they are in doubt concerning their meeting with their Lord. Surely He fully encompasses everything.

commentary.text: That is, the basis of disbelief and heedlessness is that one is unsure if we will ever meet our Lord and be held accountable for our deeds and actions. The truth is that no one can escape His grasp nor can our deeds be hidden from Him.
LESSON: EMBRACE TAWHID AND THEN PREACH/PASS IT FORWARD.

items.text: OUR DUTY AS MUSLIMS

Our duty for Muslims is to give the Quran its due or its right, which is, to recite, read and understand the Quran. In this regard Allah SWT has repeatedly stated that there is nothing confusing and/or ambiguous in the Quran that hinders understanding. It has been explained plainly as to what constitutes success and what leads to failure, what are the right beliefs and what are the wrong beliefs, what is good and what is evil, what is high morality and what is vice, in what way lies the good of man and in what he incurs loss for himself.

كِتٰبٌ فُصِّلَتۡ Fussilate: Means to separate in sections so as to make the meaning clear and distinct. Fussilate is derived from the word tafseer means to explain. The Quran is clear and detailed in its meaning and sound and wise in its rulings. Thus, the Quran is not a book of riddles, poetry, or conjecture with hidden meanings rather a clear Book of guidance/mercy/good news and warning.
Spread the message of Islam to others (dawah). Again, Allah SWT has not left us without instructions or guidance. We are told how to give dawa.
WISDOM IN DAWAH
(41:33) And who is fairer in speech than he who calls to Allah and acts righteously and says: “I am a Muslim”?
Firstly, lead by example in performing good deeds and then invite others to the worship of Allah SWT. (Dawah)

(41:34) (O Prophet), good and evil are not equal. Repel (evil) with that which is good, and you will see that he, between whom and you there was enmity, shall become as if he were a bosom friend (of yours).
The best dawah is to kill them with kindness.
BE ON YOUR GUARD AGAINST THE PROVOCATIONS OF SATAN
(41:36) And if you are prompted by a provocation from Satan, seek refuge with Allah. He, and He alone, is All-Hearing, All- Knowing.
He will incite you as a well-wisher and sincere friend. Whenever you feel an undue poking, seek Allah’s refuge by reciting the Taawwuz.
AUZUBILLAH MINASHAITAN NIRAJEEM
The meaning is “I seek refuge in Allah from the outcast Shaitan."
UNDERSTAND THE QUALITIES AND CHARACTERISTICS OF OUR RAAB SO AS NOT TO ASCRIBE FALSE ATTRIBUTES TO HIM
وَذٰلِكُمۡ ظَنُّكُمُ الَّذِىۡ ظَنَنۡتُمۡ بِرَبِّكُمۡ اَرۡدٰٮكُمۡ فَاَصۡبَحۡتُمۡ مِّنَ الۡخٰسِرِيۡن

The successful person is one who remembers death often and prepares for this eventually keeping in mind Allah SWT commands and instructions. Control worldly desires in this world, whether it is excessive sleep, heedless of salah etc., so as to achieve Heaven where all desires will be fulfilled.

The foolish person is one who follows his/her own desires in this world while ascribing false attributes to Allah SWT i.e. Allah SWT is most forgiving and too big to care about what silly ole me is doing etc.

(41:50) And if We let them taste a mercy from Us after being touched with adversity, they will certainly say, “This is what I deserve. I do not think the Hour will ˹ever˺ come. And if in fact I am returned to my Lord, the finest reward with Him will definitely be mine.” But We will surely inform the disbelievers of what they used to do. And We will certainly make them taste a harsh torment.

Thus, by receiving gifts and mercy from Allah SWT they feel they deserve it. That is, I have gotten all this because of my being worthy of it. It is my right that I should receive all this. This attitude is Kufur (disbelief).
DEFINITION OF SUCCESS

(41:8) As to those who have faith and do good works, surely theirs shall be a never-ending reward.
Iman + Good/Righteous deeds = Success

items.text: وَالَّذِيۡنَ اسۡتَجَابُوا لِرَبِّهِمۡ وَاَقَامُوۡا الصَّلٰوةَ اَمۡرُهُمۡ شُوۡرٰى بَيۡنَهُمۡ وَمِمَّا رَزَقۡنٰهُمۡ يُنۡفِقُوۡن
(42:38) Who Respond to their Lord; keep up the prayer; conduct their affairs by mutual consultation; give to others out of what We have provided for them;

front_matter.label: Note
front_matter.text: This Surah is not be confused with Surah 26, Ash-Shuarraa (The Poets).

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: This is a Makki Surah and it belongs to the group of seven Ha Mim Surahs that were revealed one after another in the middle Makkan period. This Surah has 53 Ayat in 5 Rukus.

front_matter.label: Subject and Topics
front_matter.text:
There are seven Surahs in the Quran that begin with Ha Mim and they are: (i) al-Momin (40), (ii) Ha Mim al-Sajdah (41) (iii) Ash-Shura (42) (iv) al-Zukhruf (43) (v) al-Dukhan (44) (vi) al-Jathiyah (45) (vii) al-Ahqaf (46). These seven Surahs are also called "al-Hawamim." The central theme of all these Surah's is (i) Tawhid (the exclusive worship of Allah SWT) and (ii) Da'wah which means inviting people to the EXCLUSIVE belief/worship in Allah SWT.
The theme of this Surah is Tawhid and then the Establishment of the Deen but not just at the individual level but also at the community/societal level via laws, legislation, politics etc. Quran is the means towards this end.
This Surah emphasizes that the Quran is from Allah SWT Who revealed similar messages (Books) to other Prophets and Messengers.  The religion of Allah SWT has been the same throughout history.  If Allah wanted He would have made all people into one Ummah, but He has given freedom of choice to people. In this Surah it is also mentioned that believers are those who avoid major sins and who manage their affairs via mutual consultation (Ash-Shura)
The same one Religion has been enjoined by Allah SWT for all Mankind since the beginning of creation, and all Prophets have been (i) following it, (ii) inviting others to follow it and (iii) then establishing it in their nation. However, after the death of the Prophets, some people created new creeds and divisiveness based on their own vested interests. Thus, All the different religions and creeds found in the world today have resulted from corruption of the original Divine Truth.
The Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was sent to establish, once again, the true and original Religion -- in place of the various practices and man-made religions.
It is imperative that we fully understand how great an impertinence it is against Allah SWT to adopt a man made religion and law instead of the Religion and Law enjoined by Allah SWT. You may think it is an ordinary thing and there is nothing wrong with it but in the sight of Allah SWT it is the worst kind of shirk and a grave crime whose punishment will be imposed on all those who enforce and follow their own religion on Allah SWT's earth.

sections.title: 1-9 THE HEAVENS MIGHT HAVE BROKEN APART FROM ABOVE THOSE WHO ELEVATE ALLAH'S CREATURES TO HIS RANK IF THE ANGELS WERE NOT BEGGING FORGIVENESS FOR THE RESIDENTS OF EARTH

arabic_lines: كَذٰلِكَ يُوۡحِىۡۤ اِلَيۡكَ وَاِلَى الَّذِيۡنَ مِنۡ قَبۡلِكَۙ اللّٰهُ الۡعَزِيۡزُ الۡحَكِيۡمُ

translation.text: Thus does Allah, the Most Mighty, the Most Wise reveal to you even as (He revealed) to those (Messengers) who preceded you.

commentary.text: The Revelation and Allah SWT's Might

The disbelievers of Makkah expressed wonder and doubt about how and when the Prophet (PBUH) received divine revelation. They said: ‘Does God visit him or does he visit God? Or does some dialogue take place between him and God?’

Here the disbelievers are being told: 'Allah SWT is All-Mighty and All-Wise. Whenever He pleases to have contact with a servant, nothing can obstruct His will and intention.' Lexically, 'wahi' or 'revelation' means swift and secret instruction. As a term this word has been used for the guidance and instruction that is put in the mind of a man by Allah SWT like a flash of lightning.
This very theme has been repeated in the last Ayat’s of this Surah with greater clarity and detail.

translation.text: His is all that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth; He is the Most High, the All-Great.

commentary.text: The disbelievers of Makkah's core objection to the Prophet (PBUH) and the Quran were against the concept of Tawhid (the Exclusive worship of Allah SWT) as they did not want to give up idolatry or the worship of their saints and holy men.

At this it has been said: This whole universe belongs to Allah SWT; He is the High, the Great! He is far above that somebody else should be equal to Him in rank and should become His associate in His Being, attributes, powers or rights.

translation.text: The heavens nearly burst, one above the other, in awe of Him. And the angels glorify the praises of their Lord, and seek forgiveness for those on earth. Surely Allah alone is the All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

commentary.text: It is not a trivial matter that a being is joined in lineage with Allah SWT and regarded as His son or daughter. Or to proclaim that some holy saint can help or answer the prayers of mankind.
This boldness against God is such that may well cause the heavens to break asunder. (This same theme has also been presented in (Surah Maryam, Ayats 88- 91).

And the angels shudder with fear and revulsion when they hear such garbage being uttered in respect of their Lord. They say: Glorified be Allah! None can become an associate with Allah, Lord of the worlds, in divinity and command. Therefore, they implore Allah SWT for mercy, again and again, for the dwellers of the earth that they may be spared from the torment and given respite to mend their ways.

translation.text: Those who have taken others than Him as their protectors beside Him, it is Allah Who oversees them; you are no guardian over them.

commentary.text: Taking others as 'auliya/wali' or 'guardians instead of Allah SWT means to regard them as one’s patron, supporter and helper in the four below mentioned ways:

Whom he obeys in all matters, whose instructions he carries out and whose ways and customs and rules he follows in all affairs of life (Surah An-Nisa, Ayats 118-120); (Surah Al-Aaraf, Ayats: 3,27-30);

In whose guidance he has full faith, and who he thinks will lead him aright and save him from error and deviation (Surah Al-Baqarah, Ayat 257); (Surah Bani Israil, Ayat 97); (Surah Al-Kahf, Ayats 17-50); (Surah Al-Jathiah, Ayat 19).

About whom he trusts that he will protect him from the torment of God in the Hereafter if it really existed (Surah An-Nisa, Ayats 123, 173); (Surah Al-Anaam, Ayat 51); (Surah Ar-Raad, Ayat 37); (Surah Al-Ankabut, Ayat 22); (Surah Al- Ahzab, Ayat 65); (Surah Az-Zumar, Ayat 3).

About whom he has the belief that he helps him in the world in supernatural ways, protects him from disaster and afflictions, gets him jobs, blesses him with children, and fulfills his desires and all other needs. (Surah Houd, Ayat 20); (Surah Ar-Raad, Ayat 16); (Surah Al-Ankabut, Ayat 4l).
In fact, it is Allah SWT Who is supervise/directs/watches over these false deities or guardians that man has self-appointed as his savior and or guide.

arabic_lines: وَلَوۡ شَآءَ اللّٰهُ لَجَعَلَهُمۡ اُمَّةً وَّاحِدَةً وَّلٰـكِنۡ يُّدۡخِلُ مَنۡ يَّشَآءُ فِىۡ رَحۡمَتِهٖؕ وَالظّٰلِمُوۡنَ مَا لَهُمۡ مِّنۡ وَّلِىٍّ وَّلَا نَصِيۡرٍ

translation.text: If Allah had so willed, He could have made them all a single community. But He admits whomsoever He pleases into His Mercy. As to those given to wrong-doing, they shall have none as protector or helper.

commentary.text: The Quran was revealed to serve as a Warning

If Allah SWT wanted he could have created everyone a believer and Muslim by birth. But it is Allah SWT’s will that man should be granted the freedom of choice and action. Then whoever desires and then actively strives to gain guidance shall be given guidance and whoever wants to remain astray will be allowed to go astray.

Earning Allah SWT's blessing in this world and His Paradise in the Hereafter is not an ordinary thing, which may be distributed to all regardless. Indeed, it is a blessing of such high order for which even the angels were not considered fit. That is why Allah SWT created man as a creature endowed with power, authority with vast means of His earth placed under man's control, and thus man is tested.

The one who submits and serves Allah SWT, who takes Him as his Guardian, then Allah SWT blesses him with help, guidance and the grace to pass this test, so that he may enter His Mercy. As for those who turn away from Allah SWT and instead takes others as patrons, Allah SWT has no need to become their guardian per force.

sections.title: 10-19 ISLAM IS THE SAME DEEN (WAY OF LIFE) WHICH WAS ENJOINED ON NUH, IBRAHIM, MUSA (MOSES) AND ISA (JESUS) THEY WERE ALL ORDERED TO ESTABLISH DEEN-AL-ISLAM AND DO NOT CREATE DIVISION (SECTS) IN IT

arabic_lines: وَمَا اخۡتَلَـفۡتُمۡ فِيۡهِ مِنۡ شَىۡءٍ فَحُكۡمُهٗۤ اِلَى اللّٰهِ ؕ ذٰ لِكُمُ اللّٰهُ رَبِّىۡ عَلَيۡهِ تَوَكَّلۡتُۖ وَاِلَيۡهِ اُنِيۡبُ

translation.text: The judgement on whatever you differ rests with Allah. Such is Allah, my Lord; in Him I have put all my trust and to Him I always turn in devotion.

commentary.text: Allah SWT is the Protector, Ruler and Creator
The solution is given regarding how to deal with any matter in which people differ with each other – that is -- turn to Allah SWT and the Quran.

When all sovereignty and guardianship belong to Allah SWT alone then it is for Him to rule and judge between all mutual disputes whether it is pertaining to beliefs, laws, morals, the rights of people in their mutual dealings i.e. social political and economic life etc.

Previously to accept Tawhid at the individual level one had to change ones lifestyle now we are being told that at the collective/societal level we must all submit to Allah SWT rulings and change as a whole society/ummah.
Those who restrict Allah SWT's judgment only to the Hereafter are mistaken. Below are a few examples from the Quran regarding rulings from Allah SWT.
If there arises any dispute between you about anything, refer it to Allah and the Messenger. (Surah An-Nisa, Ayat 59).

It does not behoove a believing man and a believing woman that when Allah and His Messenger have given their verdict in a matter, they should exercise an option in that matter of theirs. (Surah Al-Ahzab, Ayat 36).
This theme occurs in Ayat 24 below and has been expressed at several places in the Quran.
Also see (Surah Ar-Raad, Ayats 17,41); (Surah Ibrahim, Ayats 24-27); (Surah Bani Israil, Ayat 8); (Surah Al-Anbiya, Ayats 18, 44 and the E.Ns).
…..Such is Allah, my Lord; in Him I have put all my trust (tawakul) and to Him I always turn in devotion……
A past tense and present tense verb have been seen here that brings a sense of infinity/timelessness.

In the past verb it was said: In Whom did I put my trust, i.e. I decided once and for all that as long as I live to rely on His help, on His guidance, on His support and protection, and on His decision. Then in the present verb it was said: To Whom I turn, i.e. Whatever situation I face in life, I turn only to Allah SWT. I do not look towards others in an affliction or difficulty but invoke only Him for help and guidance. Whenever I am confronted by a problem, I seek its solution in His teaching and guidance. And I look up only to Him when I have a dispute with somebody with the belief that He alone will give the final decision, and have the faith that whatever decision He gives will be the right one.

translation.text: The Originator of the heavens and the earth, He has appointed for you pairs of your own kind, and pairs also of cattle. Thus does He multiply you. Naught in the universe is like Him. He is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.

commentary.text: Absolute and complete negation that anyone/anything is like Allah SWT.

translation.text: His are the keys of the heavens and the earth. He enlarges and straitens the sustenance of whomsoever He pleases. Surely He has knowledge of everything.

commentary.text: These are arguments to prove why Allah SWT alone is absolutely unique the true Guardian and why putting trust in Him alone is right and correct and why He alone should be turned to in all matters.
For explanation, see (Surah An-Naml, Ayats 60-66); (Surah Ar-Room, Ayats 20-22 and the E.Ns)).

arabic_lines: شَرَعَ لَـكُمۡ مِّنَ الدِّيۡنِ مَا وَصّٰى بِهٖ نُوۡحًا وَّالَّذِىۡۤ اَوۡحَيۡنَاۤ اِلَيۡكَ وَمَا وَصَّيۡنَا بِهٖۤ اِبۡرٰهِيۡمَ وَمُوۡسٰى وَعِيۡسٰٓى اَنۡ اَقِيۡمُوا الدِّيۡنَ وَ لَا تَتَفَرَّقُوۡا فِيۡهِؕ كَبُـرَ عَلَى الۡمُشۡرِكِيۡنَ مَا مَنۡ يُّنِيۡبُ تَدۡعُوۡهُمۡ اِلَيۡهِ ؕ اَللّٰهُ يَجۡتَبِىۡۤ اِلَيۡهِ مَنۡ يَّشَآءُ وَيَهۡدِىۡۤ اِلَيۡهِ

translation.text: He has prescribed for you the religion which He enjoined upon Noah and which We revealed to you (O Muhammad), and which We enjoined upon Abraham and Moses and Jesus, commanding: “Establish this religion and do not split up regarding it.” What you are calling to is very hard upon those who associate others with Allah in His Divinity. Allah chooses for Himself whomsoever He pleases and guides to Himself whoever penitently turns to Him.

commentary.text: The Religion of all the Messengers is One
This Ayat is the pinnacle of this Surah as it sheds an important light on the origins of deen (religion) and its aim. Some say it is one of the heaviest Ayat’s of the Quran.

This Ayat is addressed to the entire Islamic ummah to establish deen. What has already been mentioned in the first Ayat is being further elaborated here. Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) is not the founder of any new religion, nor were any previous Prophets founders of a separate religion, rather it has been one and the same religion (deen) that all the Prophets have been presenting from the very beginning.

Thus, from the beginning of time we are all MUSLIM (meaning we submit to one God). We are all born on the fitra of deen (meaning innately we are all born Muslim). Allah SWT sent messengers and Books to guide humanity to the right path i.e. Torah, Bible, Quran. Yet, after knowledge was revealed, men invented their own creed due to arrogance, stubbornness and pride. For example, the Jewish priests, in order to retain their power, would hide and even alter Allah SWT teachings from the common man. Another example of inventions is religion is because man is a slave to his desire thus, he will invent innovations in religion, for example, that is fine to say fajr prayers whenever you wake up and not necessary to say it at the prescribed time etc.

Lexically, the word sharaa is a road/highway i.e. Shara e faisal. Allah SWT has carved out a roadmap for man that shows us the pathway to life.  شَرَعَ لَكُم Sharaa lakum (prescribed/ordained for you all) implies appointing a way, a code and a rule. From sharaa we get the word shariat understood as the synonym for legislation and law.

Although, all Prophets including but not limited to Prophet Nuh, Ibrahim, Isa, Musa and Muhammad (PBU them all) brought one and the same religion, the shariat was different. The Prophets were given instruction: أَقِيمُوا الدِّينَ Aqim-ud-din; “The word 'iqamat' from the word 'qaaim' or 'to establish implies: (i) lead by example (ii) give dawah (iii) and enforce deen practically at the societal level via rules and laws.

So when the Prophets were enjoined to establish the deen and to keep it established, it did not simply mean that (i) they should practice it themselves and (ii) preach it to others so that the people may accept its truth, but also that (iii) when people have accepted it, steps should be taken to introduce and enforce the deen practically into society by building mosques, eliminating usury from governance etc., so that Islam becomes an integral part of peoples lives.

The Prophet (PBUH) during the 23 years of his Prophethood established a full-fledged system of governance in Arabia, encompassing all aspects of life, from personal beliefs and conduct to collective morality, culture and civilization, economic and social life, politics and judiciary, peace and war. Thus the definition of iqamat deen (establishment of deen) was beautifully executed.

Whoever studies the Quran carefully will see that this Book does not envisage that its adherents live as subjects of the disbelievers rather it demands from its followers that they should struggle with their lives for intellectual, cultural, legal and political supremacy of the true faith.

Thus, deen refers not only to the acceptance of Tawhid, the Hereafter, the Book, the Prophet hood, the performance of certain acts of devotion to Allah SWT but must also include the Islamic shariat commandments, (rules and regulations.) For, if sharia (law) is something separate from deen (religion) and the command is only for establishing the deen and not the sharia, inevitably the Muslims, like the Christians, would regard the sharia as unimportant and remain content with only beliefs and a few universal moral principles.

As for the differences in the shariah, it does not mean that the shariahs sent by God were mutually contradictory rather it means that in their details there have been some differences owing to the different environments, for instance, the prayer and the fast. The prayer has been obligatory in all shariahs but there have been differences regarding the qiblah, timings and rakahs. Likewise, fasting was obligatory in every shariah, however, the month long fasting of Ramadan is only found in Islam.
Thus, to perform the prayer and observe the fast according to the rules and procedures (shariah) of every Prophet amounted to establishment of deen at that time.

Instead of speculation, let us turn to the Quran itself and see whether the deen that we have been enjoined to establish implies only beliefs and a few universally important moral principles only, or the shariah values and commandments as well:

And the only command they were given was to worship Allah, making their deen sincerely His, turning all their attention towards Him, and to establish the Salat and to pay the Zakat, this alone is the true and right deen. (Surah Al-Bayyinah, Ayat 5).

You are forbidden carrion and blood, the flesh of swine and of that animal which has been slaughtered in any name other than of Allah, and of the strangled animal, and of that beaten to death or killed by a fall or gored to death or mangled by a beast of prey, save of that you duly slaughtered while it was still alive, and of that which is slaughtered at (ungodly) shrines. It is also unlawful for you to try to find your fortune by means of divining devices, for all these things are sinful acts. Today the disbelievers have despaired of (vanquishing) your religion; therefore do not fear them but fear Me. Today I have perfected your deen for you and completed My blessing on you and approved Islam as the deen (way of life) for you. (Surah Al-Maidah, Ayat 3).

Fight with those from among the people of the Book, who do not believe in Allah nor in the Last Day; who do not make unlawful what Allah and His Messenger have made unlawful, and do not adopt the right deen as their deen. (Surah At-Taubah, Ayat 29).

The woman and the man guilty of fornication, flog each one of them with a hundred stripes, and let not any pity for them restrain you in regard to a matter prescribed in the deen of Allah, if you believe in Allah and the Last Day. (Surah An-Noor, Ayat 2).

The Ayat above shows that criminal law is also deen. If a man follows the criminal law prescribed by God, he is a follower of God’s deen and if he follows a king’s law, he is a follower of the king’s deen.
After giving the command for 'iqamat deen', Allah SWT states that : لَا تَتَفَرَّقُوا فِيهِ La tatafarraqu fihi: Do not create splits or divides in the deen. Creating schisms in deen implies:
To introduce something entirely new into deen.
To exclude from deen something which actually belonged to it.
To tamper with the fundamentals of deen by misinterpretations and introduce new beliefs and novel practices.
To distort the deen by making changes of fundamental nature, for example, by reducing what is important to un-important, or making something optional as obligatory etc.
Owing to such innovations, divisions first appeared in the communities of the Prophets; then gradually various sects developed into separate and mutually exclusive religious systems.

FYI -- These divisions have nothing to do with the permissible and reasonable differences of opinion which naturally takes place among the scholars when they are engaged in understanding and studying the injunctions and fundamentals of deen.

For a detailed discussion of this subject, see ( Surah Al-Baqarah, Ayat 213); (Surah Aal-Imran, Ayats 19, 50); (Surah An-Nisa, Ayat 171); (Surah Al-Maidah, Ayat 77); (Surah Al-Anaam, Ayat 159); (Surah An-Nahl, Ayats 118-124); (Surah Al- Anbiya, Ayats 92-93); (Surah Al-Hajj, Ayat 67); (Surah Al- Muminun, Ayats 53-54); (Surah Al-Qasas, Ayat 53); (Surah ArRoom, Ayat 32 and the E.Ns).

translation.text: They divided, out of rivalry, only after knowledge had come to them, and, if it had not been for a decree already passed by your Lord to reprieve them until an appointed time, they would already have been judged. Those after them, who inherited the Scripture, are in disquieting doubt about it.

commentary.text: Divisions created in deen were not because Allah SWT failed to send Prophets and the Books, therefore, people invented their own separate religions, sects, schools and systems of life, but divisions appeared after knowledge had come from Allah SWT. The motive for creating divisions stemmed from the desire
and greed for worldly wealth and position, mutual rivalries, stubbornness, arrogance etc.

In the case of the Torah and the Gospel, earlier generations did not convey both these Books to the later generations in their original state, words and language. Rather, they mixed up the 'Divine word' with the 'human word' in the form of their own commentary and interpretation. In fact they made their translations so prevail that the original was lost and only the translations remain. Thus, people now are merely imitating their forefathers, without any evidence or proof, causing confusion and doubt.
Lesson: Do not blindly follow your ancestors, societal norms or desires. Develop firm conviction in all matters of religion by educating yourself. Gain knowledge of the Quran and Hadith.

translation.text: (This being so, O Muhammad), (1) call people to the same religion and (2) be steadfast about it as you were commanded, and (3) do not follow their desires, and (4) say (to them): “I believe in the Book Allah has sent down. (5) I have been commanded to establish justice among you. (6) Allah is our Lord and your Lord. (7) We have our deeds and you have your deeds. (8) There is no contention between us and you. (9) Allah will bring us all together. (10) To Him all are destined to return.”

commentary.text: This Ayah includes ten separate and independent ideas, each of which is a ruling on its own:

Invite people to the religion of peace (Islam) –Same religion means belief in only one God whether Jews, Christians, or Muslims we all have the same religion i.e. Tawhid, belief in the Hereafter, belief in Prophets. (Give Dawah)
Adhere firmly and steadfastly to the worship of Allah SWT as He has commanded you. (Lead by example)

Do not make any modifications or compromises in religion so as to accommodate people's (disbelievers) desires, whims, prejudices and practices of ignorance, in the hope that they will embrace Islam. (Do not make innovations in religion)

The belief in all the Books that have been revealed to the Prophets is mandatory; we cannot differentiate between any of them. Do not cause division in religion. (Reiterate similarities when giving dawah).
Judgment should be according to the commands of Allah SWT. Only Allah SWT will decide and Judge. (Do not make self-proclamations regarding who is a good Muslim and who will go to Heaven/Hell, etc.)
Allah SWT is the One Who is to be worshipped, and there is no true God but He. (Message of Tawhid)

Each one of us is responsible and accountable for our deeds whether good or evil. The same thing has been stated in (Surah Younus, Ayat 41); And if they deny you, say: "For me are my deeds and for you are your deeds! You are innocent of what I do, and I am innocent of what you do!'' (Accept Islam as it is for your own good.)

We have done our best in conveying to you the message. Now there is no use in arguing and disputing, therefore, even if you try to have a dispute with us, we have no desire to join in. (Focus Dawah efforts on those who are receptive. Do not argue or dispute with those who are intent on disbelieving.)
On the Day of Judgment Allah SWT will gather us all together.  (Soon the truth will be clear).
The final return on the Day of Reckoning. (Always remember death and to whom we will be answerable).

sections.title: 20-29 HE WHO DESIRES THE HARVEST IN THE HEREAFTER SHALL BE GIVEN MANY FOLDS, BUT HE WHO DESIRES IN THIS LIFE SHALL BE GIVEN A PORTION HERE BUT SHALL HAVE NO SHARE IN THE HEREAFTER

translation.text: Whoever seeks the harvest of the Hereafter, We shall increase for him his harvest, and whoever seeks the harvest of this world, We shall give him thereof; but he will have no share in the Hereafter.

commentary.text: This is a very important concept that we must understand in order to define and determine our attitude towards life.
In a beautiful simile, both the seeker of the Hereafter and the seeker of the world have been likened to the farmer, who puts in all his labor so that he may reap what he has sowed.

As for the farmer who is sowing or striving for the Hereafter, he will get a share of this world, i.e. what has already been decreed for him, however, Allah SWT has not given him the good news of the harvest of this world. Rather, the good news is that since he is a seeker of the Hereafter then Allah SWT helps facilitate and increase this correct intention, for example, if he is performing good deeds with sincere intentions, he will be blessed with the grace to do more righteous deeds and when he makes up his mind to adopt pure means for achieving pure aims, he will be blessed with pure means only.
As for the one who is only sowing for this world, and not at all concerned about the Hereafter, Allah SWT has plainly told him the results of his labors:
(1) That, however hard he may struggle, he will not get the whole of what he is trying for, but only a fraction of it i.e. that which Allah SWT has ordained for him.
(2) That whatever he has to get, he will get in this world and there is no share for him of the good things in the Hereafter.
FYI -- In fact, every person whether good or bad, is getting his sustenance here.
Lesson: Become a talib or seeker of Hereafter so that you can gain khair (good) in both worlds.

They will have whatever they desire from their Lord. That is ˹truly˺ the greatest bounty.

sections.title: 30-43 WHATEVER AFFLICTIONS BEFALL UPON PEOPLE ARE THE RESULT OF THEIR OWN MISDEEDS AND TRUE BELIEVERS ARE THOSE WHO ESTABLISH SALAH, GIVE CHARITY AND DEFEND THEMSELVES WHEN OPPRESSED

translation.text: Whatever misfortune befalls you is a consequence of your own deeds. But much of it He forgives.

commentary.text: The Cause of Misfortune is Sin

One should note that here the cause of all human afflictions is not being stated rather this address is directed to the people of Makkah who were at that time committing disbelief and disobedience. They are being told: 'The calamities, including the famine of Makkah, are a warning so that you may take heed and examine your actions.'

For further explanation it is necessary to state that for the sincere believer, Allah SWT’s law is  different. All calamities and hardships that befall a believer serve as a atonement for his sins, errors and deficiencies. There is an authentic Hadith to the effect: Whatever sorrow and suffering, distress, grief, affliction and worry a Muslim experiences, even if it be a thorn prick, it is made an atonement by Allah SWT for one of his errors. (Bukhari, Muslim). As for the hardships that a believer faces in the way of raising Allah SWT’s Word, they do not merely become an atonement for his deficiencies but also a means of the exaltation of ranks with Allah SWT.

translation.text: What you have been given is only the fleeting enjoyment of this world. Far better and more lasting is what God will give to those who believe and trust in their Lord;

commentary.text: DEFINITION OF SUCCESS
Iman + Trust in Allah SWT (tawakul) = Success
Attributes of those people who want to establish religion (deen) are provided in these 8 Ayats (42:36 till 42: 43)

For people who want to establish religion the characteristics and priorities required are being mentioned. First characteristic is: (i) Tawakul or complete trust in Allah SWT and (ii) complete disinterest in this world thus decide to become a seeker of the Hereafter and not this world.

The world with all its glamour and distractions does not divert them from their mission to establish the deen because they are not invested in this world rather the Hereafter is their main focus. Here, trust (tawakul) in Allah SWT has been regarded as an inevitable demand of faith and a necessary characteristic for success in the Hereafter.
Tawakul means:

(1) That man should have full confidence that the guidance, principles, laws, rules and regulations that Allah SWT had enjoined upon us are based on divine truth and in following them lies our salvation and well being.

(2) That man should rely only on Allah SWT and not his own or other peoples powers, abilities, means, resources, plans, schemes and help. Success in this life and in the Hereafter depends upon the help and succor of Allah SWT.

(3) That man should have complete faith in the promises that Allah SWT has made with those who adopt righteousness and discard the benefits, gains and pleasures that accrue from following the way of falsehood, and patiently endure losses, hardships and deprivations along this path.

From this explanation of the meaning of tawakkul it becomes obvious how deeply it is related with faith, and why those wonderful results that have been promised to the believers who actively strive and practice tawakkul cannot be obtained from the mere/empty affirmation of faith.

translation.text: Who shun great sins and gross indecencies; who forgive when they are angry;

commentary.text: For people who want to establish religion the characteristics and priorities required are being mentioned. They (i) steer clear of big sins, such as taking riba, stealing, lying etc., (ii) and from acts of shamelessness such as zina (iii) control their anger and learn to forgive people.  Only then one can take worship to the next level.

'Those who forgive when they are angry,' possess one of the best qualities of man, which has been highly commended in the Quran (Surah Aal-Imran, Ayat 134) and regarded as a major factor of the Prophet’s (PBUH) success (Surah Aal-Imran, Ayat 159). According to Aishah, the Messenger of Allah (PBUH) never avenged himself on anybody, however, when a thing enjoined to be held sacred by Allah SWT was desecrated, he would award the punishment. (Bukhari, Muslim).
For explanation, see (Surah An-Nisa, Ayat 31); (Surah Al-Anaam, Ayat 151); (Surah An-Naml, Ayat 90); (Surah An- Najm, Ayat 32 and the E.Ns).

arabic_lines: وَالَّذِيۡنَ اسۡتَجَابُوا لِرَبِّهِمۡ وَاَقَامُوۡا الصَّلٰوةَ اَمۡرُهُمۡ شُوۡرٰى بَيۡنَهُمۡ وَمِمَّا رَزَقۡنٰهُمۡ يُنۡفِقُوۡن

translation.text: Who Respond to their Lord; keep up the prayer; conduct their affairs by mutual consultation; give to others out of what We have provided for them;

commentary.text: For people who want to establish religion the characteristics and priorities required are being mentioned. “Those who respond or answer the call of their Lord,” means that they hasten to do whatever Allah SWT has enjoined them to do – thus far in this Surah it is to (i) hasten to establish the deen (ii) And they establish salah in essence their connection to Allah SWT (iii) And they work to establish the deen with mutual consultation (iv) And they spend in the cause of Allah SWT.

Allah SWT has given the Muslim Ummah the mission of living up to this Deen and then sharing it with others. This responsibility means that Muslims have to learn to work with each other whether it be to build a mosque or school etc. Mutual consultation (Shura) means respect, open communication, listening, shared decision-making and collaboration.

A great quality of the believer and an important pillar of the Islamic way of life is mentioned here and also in ( Surah Aal-Imran, Ayat 159) which is: 'consultation'. The Islamic way of life requires that the principle of consultation be employed in every collective affair, big or small. If it is a domestic matter, the husband and wife should act via mutual consultation and when the children have grown up they should also be consulted. If it is a matter concerning the whole family, the opinion of every adult member should be solicited. Thus, in every matter where more than one person is involved, all concerned parties should be consulted and their opinions valued, respected and taken into account.

Allah SWT then calls upon those of us who want to establish Allah SWT's deen, to spend on projects to serve the Deen. Invest in the mission to spread Islam, whether it be money, time, youth etc, whatever is most precious to you. Give from what you love.

translation.text: who, defend themselves when they are oppressed.

commentary.text: Another characteristic of the believers who want to establish deen is that they do not fall prey to tyrants and they do not accept humiliation, abuse and disgrace.

Important to note that when giving da'wah one has to adopt a very gentle and non-confrontational stance. However when it comes to the establishment of deen there can be no compromises. Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) in Makkah was very different from Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) of Madina.

translation.text: The recompense of evil is evil the like of it. But he who forgives and makes amends, his reward lies with Allah. Surely, He does not love the wrong-doers.
There is no blame on those who enforce justice after being wronged.
Blame is only on those who wrong people and transgress in the land unjustly. It is they who will suffer a painful punishment.
Though if a person is patient and forgives, this is one of the greatest things.

commentary.text: For such people who want to establish religion priorities are being mentioned. Ayat 42:40 till 42:43 stress the same concept that take revenge if you want. But to forgive is divine.
Forgiving or exacting Revenge on Wrongdoers

The first and most fundamental principle re: retaliation is the correct limit of retaliation; that one should not exceed the ill treatment received and thus become a wrongdoer himself in the process of avenging a wrong. It is not permissible to do a greater wrong in retaliation for the wrong committed, for example, if a person gives another a slap, the other can return only one slap; he cannot shower blows and kicks. Likewise, it is not right to commit a sin in retaliation for a sin. For example, if a wicked man has killed someone's son then it is not right to go and kill the son of the former.
The second principle regarding retaliation is that although it is permissible to retaliate against the one who has committed an injustice, yet, pardoning is better for the sake of reconcilement.

sections.title: 44-48 THE REAL LOSERS ARE THOSE WHO WILL LOSE ON THE DAY OF RESURRECTION

translation.text: And you will see them exposed to the Fire, fully humbled out of disgrace, stealing glances ˹at it˺. And the believers will say, “The ˹true˺ losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on Judgment Day.” The wrongdoers will certainly be in everlasting torment.

commentary.text: DEFINITION OF LOSERS

The state of those who will be driven into Hell has been depicted here. By nature, man is such that when a dreadful scene comes before him, he can only steal glances at his dreadful and everlasting fate.

sections.title: 49-50 IT IS ALLAH WHO GIVES DAUGHTERS AND SONS AS HE PLEASES

translation.text: To Allah ˹alone˺ belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth. He creates whatever He wills. He blesses whoever He wills with daughters, and blesses whoever He wills with sons
or grants them a mix of males and females, and causes whomever He pleases to be barren. He is All- Knowing, All-Powerful.

commentary.text: This is a manifest proof of Allah SWT’s Sovereignty being absolute. No man has ever been able to produce an offspring. The one whom Allah SWT makes barren cannot have children through any medicine, any treatment, any amulet or charm. The one whom Allah SWT gives only daughters cannot produce a single son by any device, and the one whom Allah SWT gives only sons cannot have a single daughter by any means. In this matter everyone is absolutely helpless. Even after appreciating all this if someone postures to be all-powerful in God’s kingdom or regards another as the possessor of powers, it would be his own shortsightedness for which he himself will suffer.

sections.title: 51-53 IT IS NOT VOUCHSAFED FOR ANY HUMAN BEING THAT ALLAH SHOULD SPEAK TO HIM FACE TO FACE

translation.text: It is not possible to any human being that Allah should speak to him except through revelation/inspiration, or from behind a veil, or that a messenger (an angel) be sent to him who reveals to him by Allah's leave whatever He wishes. He is All-High, Most Wise.

commentary.text: This Ayat is the most important re: the reality and variety of how revelation comes down

In conclusion, the same theme with which the discourse began has been reiterated. To understand it fully, please see again Ayat (42:3) Thus does Allah, the Most Mighty, the Most Wise reveal to you even as (He revealed) to those (Messengers) who preceded you.

Here the Jews asked the Holy Prophet (PBUH), "How can we believe in you when you neither see Allah SWT, nor do you speak to Him face to face, as Prophet Musa (PBUH) used to see and converse with Allah SWT?" Then this Ayat was revealed to announce that it is not possible nor befitting for any human being to converse with Allah SWT face to face in this world.
There are only three ways in which Allah SWT speaks to a human being:

(i) One is ` wahi' which is the infusion of something in the heart. It can happen while one is awake and or it can also happen during sleep in the form of a dream as stated in many hadith that the Holy Prophet (PBUH) said, 'This has been infused in my heart.' Or like the mother of Musa (PBUH) felt she must put her baby in the river for him to be safe. 
(ii) The second way in which Allah SWT may address a person, is that Allah SWT speaks from behind a veil/curtain, as happened with Prophet Musa (PBUH) on Mount Tur.
(iii) The third method is that He sends a messenger. The messenger can be angel Jibra'il or any other angel who may carry Allah SWT's message and read it out to the Prophet. This has been the most common way. The entire Quran has been revealed in this way through angels.

arabic_lines: وَكَذٰلِكَ اَوۡحَيۡنَاۤ اِلَيۡكَ رُوۡحًا مِّنۡ اَمۡرِنَا ؕ مَا كُنۡتَ تَدۡرِىۡ مَا الۡكِتٰبُ وَلَا الۡاِيۡمَانُ وَلٰـكِنۡ جَعَلۡنٰهُ نُوۡرًا نَّهۡدِىۡ بِهٖ مَنۡ نَّشَآءُ مِنۡ عِبَادِنَا ؕ وَاِنَّكَ لَتَهۡدِىۡۤ اِلٰى صِرَاطٍ مُّسۡتَقِيۡمٍۙ

translation.text: And so We have sent to you ˹O Prophet˺ a revelation by Our command. You did not know of ˹this˺ Book and faith ˹before˺. But We have made it a light, by which We guide whoever We will of Our servants. And you are truly leading ˹all˺ to the Straight Path—

commentary.text: The Quran is the Nur/Ruh from which mankind gets guidance. Thus, our Ruh will only get peace when we are at one with the Quran (Nur/Ruh). When light meets light. Origin of the word Ruh means contentment and peace. We were in perfect contentment when we were with our Lord and in this world, we find unrest and discontent till we read/recite and understand the Quran.
FYI – Our fitra or Ruh is dormant till the Quran makes it complete and active. We are spiritually meaningless without the Quran.

The Prophet has been given knowledge of the Quran and now is our guide so as to direct us to the straight path. (FYI –couldn’t be easier to guide to the straight path as opposed to a crooked path.) But only Allah SWT is the ultimate Guider and if Allah SWT guides/blesses us with the Quran then that is our ultimate good fortunate.

translation.text: the Way of Allah, to Whom belongs the dominion of all that is in the heavens and the earth. Lo, it is to Allah that all things ultimately revert.

commentary.text: Allah SWT establishes His complete ownership in these last few Ayat’s, that is, whether we have children or not, who will be guided or not, when the messenger gets revelation etc. are all in Allah SWT's control.
Every decision we make in this world will be presented before Allah SWT and ultimately He will decide the fate of every person. No consultation needed!
CHOOSE WISELY! Every decision has consequences in this world as well as the next.

Lesson: Now that you have heard and understood then ACT INSTANTLY without delay (meaning don’t wait for the opportune time i.e. once the kids have grown up or once I am a bit older or once I am done with my studies etc – only then I will focus on my religion and help with the establishment of deen -- because there are no guarantees you will be alive then.
Project Islam in the best possible manner and lead by example. Give dawah wisely so that people are not offended and move away from deen.

items.text: Every Surah has its own/unique core concept and it is up to us to search out and understand these key themes. Within this Madani surah the crucial idea is that of the establishment of deen أَقِيمُوا الدِّينَ Aqim-ud-din.

The important Ayat’s that convey this theme are: Ayat 10: All judgment is with Allah SWT. Ayat 13 to 15: Establish deen and do not have any differences in this regard. Ayat 36 to 43. Attributes of those who want to establish deen are that (i) he/she is a seeker of the Hereafter and hence this world is not an allure or distraction (ii) Tawakul (reliance or trust) is solely upon Allah SWT and not on one's own or anyone else's abilities, intellect etc. (iii) they stay away from the Big Sins and from all indecencies and keep their anger in control. They establish prayer and perform jihad with their money, abilities etc., in an effort to establish the deen. And lastly, the exact revenge when required but forgiveness in much better.
A. The important Ayat’s that convey this theme are: Ayat 10: All judgment is with Allah SWT.
(42:10) The judgement on whatever you differ rests with Allah. Such is Allah, my Lord; in Him I have put all my trust and to Him I always turn in devotion.
B. Ayat 13 to 15: Establish deen (religion) and do not have any differences in this regard. Be steadfast and do not follow the disbelievers.

(42:13) He has prescribed for you the religion which He enjoined upon Noah and which We revealed to you (O Muhammad), and which We enjoined upon Abraham and Moses and Jesus, commanding: “Establish this religion and do not split up regarding it.” What you are calling to is very hard upon those who associate others with Allah in His Divinity. Allah chooses for Himself whomsoever He pleases and guides to Himself whoever penitently turns to Him.

(42:14) They divided, out of rivalry, only after knowledge had come to them, and, if it had not been for a decree already passed by your Lord to reprieve them until an appointed time, they would already have been judged. Those after them, who inherited the Scripture, are in disquieting doubt about it.

(42:15) (This being so, O Muhammad), (1) call people to the same religion and (2) be steadfast about it as you were commanded, and (3) do not follow their desires, and (4) say (to them): “I believe in the Book Allah has sent down. (5) I have been commanded to establish justice among you. (6) Allah is our Lord and your Lord. (7) We have our deeds and you have your deeds. (8) There is no contention between us and you. (9) Allah will bring us all together. (10) To Him all are destined to return.”
C. Ayat 36 to 43 – although the first three Ayat’s here are the most relevant.
Attributes of those who want to establish deen are that:
(42:36) What you have been given is only the fleeting enjoyment of this world. Far better and more lasting is what God will give to those who believe and trust in their Lord;

He/she is a seeker of the Hereafter and hence this world is not an allure or distraction and tawakul (reliance or trust) is solely upon Allah SWT and not on one's own or anyone else's abilities, intellect etc.
(42:37) Who shun great sins and gross indecencies; who forgive when they are angry;

They stay away from the Big Sins and from all indecencies and keep their anger/rage in control. They establish prayer and perform jihad with their money, abilities etc., in an effort to establish the deen. And lastly, active resistance meaning when required they exact revenge but forgiveness in much better.
(42:38) Who Respond to their Lord; keep up the prayer; conduct their affairs by mutual consultation; give to others out of what We have provided for them;

They hasten to establish the deen (ii) And they establish salah in essence their connection to Allah SWT (iii) And they work to establish the deen with mutual consultation (iv) And they spend in the cause of Allah SWT.
Then the Ayat’s 42:39 till 42:43 the same theme is repeated that is that active struggle is now required for the establishment of the deen meaning an eye for an eye is now allowed.

Professor Montgomery Ward has highlighted this idea in his book – that Muhammad (PBUH) at Makkah was different i.e. at the time of inviting people to Islam he was gentle, mild and never related however Muhammad (PBUH) at Madinah was different because this was the time of establishment of religion so retaliation, resistance and revenge are allowed with no compromises. (Needless to say, this is only  undertaken when injustice has been committed.)

Iman + Good deed = Success
(42:26) He responds to those who believe and do good deeds, and gives them more of His bounty; agonizing torment awaits the disbelievers.
