front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text:
The name of this Surah Zukhruf-an is mentioned in Ayat 35.
(Name of Surah mentioned وَزُخْرُفًا zukhruf-an )

items.text: وَزُخۡرُفًا ؕ وَاِنۡ كُلُّ ذٰ لِكَ لَمَّا مَتَاعُ الۡحَيٰوةِ الدُّنۡيَا ؕ وَالۡاٰخِرَةُ عِنۡدَ رَبِّكَ لِلۡمُتَّقِيۡنَ
(43:35) or that they be made of gold وَزُخْرُفًا.  Surely all this is only the enjoyment of the life of the world. But (true prosperity) in the Hereafter with Your Lord is only for the God-fearing.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: It was revealed in the middle Makkan period. It has 89 Ayat’s in 7 rukus. This is from among the group of Surahs that begin with the word Ha Mim.

front_matter.label: Subject and Topics
front_matter.text:
There are seven Surahs in the Quran that begin with Ha Mim and they are:  (i) al-Momin (40), (ii) Ha Mim al-Sajdah (41) (iii) al-Shura (42) (iv) al-Zukhruf (43) (v) al-Dukhan (44) (vi) al-Jathiyah (45) (vii) al-Ahqaf (46). These seven Surahs are also called "al-Hawamim".  The central theme of all these Surah's is (i) Tawhid (the exclusive worship of Allah SWT) and (ii) Da'wah which means inviting people to the EXCLUSIVE belief/worship in Allah SWT.
The Surah tells us that the revelation (Quran) is a mercy from Allah SWT. Allah SWT chooses whosoever He wills to give His revelation.  The worldly goods and riches are inconsequential and meaningless in the sight of Allah SWT.  Real value comes from following the truth and from righteousness. This Surah is a pair with the next Surah Ad-Dukhan and both contain the exact same two beginning Ayats. A vivid description of Heaven and Hell is provided.

sections.title: 1-8 AL-QURAN IS A TRANSCRIPT FROM THE MOTHER BOOK WHICH IS IN ALLAH'S KEEPING

arabic_lines: حمٓ.

translation.text: Ha'. Mim.

arabic_lines: وَالۡكِتٰبِ الۡمُبِيۡنِ

translation.text: By the Clear Book;

commentary.text: This is not a Book of riddles rather a Book that is clear in its meaning, a Book of guidance that clarifies right from wrong. And a means of establishing a direct link/connection with our Rabb.

translation.text: verily We have made it an Arabic Qur'an that you may understand.

arabic_lines: وَاِنَّهٗ فِىۡۤ اُمِّ الۡكِتٰبِ لَدَيۡنَا لَعَلِىٌّ حَكِيۡمٌؕ

translation.text: Indeed it is transcribed in the Original Book with Us; sublime and full of wisdom.

commentary.text: 'Umm al-Kitab' means the “Original Book”, the Book from which all the Books sent down to the Prophets have been derived. In Surah Al-Waqiah the same thing has been described as 'Kitab-um-Maknun' (the hidden and preserved Book) and in (Surah Al-Burooj, Ayat 22 ) as 'Lauh-i Mahfuz' (the preserved tablet).

Numerous Books had been revealed by Allah SWT in different ages and languages to various Prophets for the guidance nations. All these Books invite mankind to one and the same faith. They presented one and the same criterion of good and evil. They propounded the same principles of morality and civilization. In short, they brought one and the same Deen (religion). Their source and origin were the same, only words were different; they had the same meaning and theme which is inscribed in a Source Book with Allah SWT, and whenever there was a need, He raised a Prophet and sent down the same meaning and subject-matter clothed in a particular diction according to the environment and occasion.

sections.title: 9-15 EVEN THE MUSHRIKEEN BELIEVE THAT HEAVENS, EARTH AND ALL THEREIN IS CREATED BY ALLAH AND SUPPLICATION BEFORE RIDING A CONVEYANCE

translation.text: Yet if you were to ask them: “Who created the heavens and the earth?” they will certainly say: “The All-Mighty, the All-Knowing has created them.”

commentary.text: The idolators acknowledge that Allah SWT is the Sole Creator of the Universe, yet, they ascribe partners to Him whether it be in the form of money, jobs, family, etc. Thus, they have a problem with the exclusive worship of Allah SWT or the concept Tauhid,

translation.text: He Who created these pairs, all of them, and provided you

commentary.text: ships and cattle on which you ride,

Pairs here does not imply only pairs of men and women among human beings and of males and females among animals and vegetation, but there are countless other things which the Creator has made as matching partners e.g. the negative and positive charges in electricity whose coming together is causing wonderful things to happen in the world.

arabic_lines: لِتَسۡتَوٗا عَلٰى ظُهُوۡرِهٖ ثُمَّ تَذۡكُرُوۡا نِعۡمَةَ رَبِّكُمۡ اِذَا اسۡتَوَيۡتُمۡ عَلَيۡهِ وَتَقُوۡلُوۡا
سُبْحانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ

translation.text: so that when you are mounted upon them you may remember the bounty of your Lord, and say: “Glory be to Him Who has subjected this to Us whereas we did not have the strength to subdue it.

commentary.text: DUA BEFORE TRAVEL (43:13 & 43:14)

Among all the creatures on earth only humans have been given the power/superiority to use animals and vehicles for bigger and stronger than man as means of transportation/conveyance. Thus, man should reflect and be grateful to the One who enabled him to steer ships in the mighty oceans, drive big metal cars, and ride animals far stronger than him but whose nature has been made subservient to man. Thus, this is a dua of humility.
To benefit by these blessings and forget the Benefactor is a sign of the heart becoming dead/ungrateful.
Whenever the Prophet (PBUH) sat on a conveyance for a journey, he would pronounce Allahu-Akbar three times, then he would recite this Ayat.

The literal meaning of this Ayat: “Perfect is Allah who has made for us subservient and subjected these means for us. Otherwise, we could not have subdued it ourselves. It is to our Lord that we shall eventually return.”

arabic_lines: وَاِنَّاۤ اِلٰى رَبِّنَا لَمُنۡقَلِبُوۡنَ

translation.text: It is to our Lord that we shall eventually return.”

commentary.text: Let us also consider the moral aspects of this teaching. Can one imagine that a person who while sitting in a conveyance starts his journey consciously with the full remembrance of Allah SWT would commit sins and injustices on the way?
THIS IS THE DUA FOR TRAVEL WHETHER IT BE A CAR, TRAIN, PLANE OR SUBWAY.
This is a way of making travel worship as the entire journey become ibadah (worship)

بِسۡمِ اللهِ الرَّحۡمٰنِ الرَّحِيۡمِ (i)
سُبْحانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ (ii)
وَاِنَّاۤ اِلٰى رَبِّنَا لَمُنۡقَلِبُوۡنَ
Tasheeh (iii)
And then istakfar (ask for forgiveness) (iv)
Above four steps are the etiquette of travel.

arabic_lines: وَجَعَلُوۡا لَهٗ مِنۡ عِبَادِهٖ جُزۡءًا ؕ اِنَّ الۡاِنۡسَانَ لَـكَفُوۡرٌ مُّبِيۡنٌ

translation.text: Yet they have made some of His servants a part of Him. Indeed man is most evidently thankless.

sections.title: 16-25 SOME MUSHRIKEEN REGARD THE ANGELS TO BE THE FEMALE DIVINITIES BEING THE DAUGHTERS OF ALLAH

translation.text: Has Allah taken for Himself daughters out of those whom He creates and has chosen you to have sons?

commentary.text: Condemnation of the Idolators ascribing Offspring to Allah SWT
Here, the folly of the polytheists of Arabia has been fully exposed. They said that the angels were the daughters of Allah SWT and carved out their images as females whom they worshiped.

About this Allah SWT says: In spite of recognizing that the Creator of the earth and heavens is Allah SWT yet you have taken others as gods/deities beside Him. Furthermore, you assign to Allah SWT the kind of offspring which you regard as disgraceful for yourselves. When a daughter is born in your house, your face grows dark, you feel distressed and sometimes you bury her alive. Yet, this is the very offspring you assign to Allah SWT and reserve for yourselves the sons, whom you regard as a source of joy and pride.

translation.text: (They believe so although when) any of them is given tidings of the birth of a female child the like of which he assigns to the Merciful One, his countenance darkens and he is choked with grief.

commentary.text: You (the Arabs) have assigned to Allah SWT the offspring that is by nature delicate, weak and frail, and adopted for yourselves the offspring that you feel is bold, courageous and fearless.

translation.text: Do they assign to Allah one who grows up amidst ornaments and is not well-versed in the art of disputation?

commentary.text: This Ayat confirms the permissibility of ornaments for women, for Allah SWT has mentioned that ornaments are a natural item for women.
Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) took silk in one hand and gold in the other and said that both were forbidden in the dress by the men of his ummah but made lawful for the women of his ummah.
Zakat must be paid in full on gold.

translation.text: In fact, they say, “We found our forefathers following a ˹particular˺ way, and we are following in their footsteps.”
And thus it is: whenever We sent any warner to a city its affluent ones said: “We found our forefathers on a way and we continue to follow in their footsteps.”

commentary.text: Here, the point worth considering is why predominantly the well to do people of every community have resisted the Prophets and upheld the imitation of their forefathers in every age.

(i) The affluent people are usually so absorbed in making and enjoying the world that they are not inclined towards the pursuit of the truth. Their love of ease and hence mental lethargy renders them heedless towards religion and more interested in preserving the established order, no matter whether it is based on truth or falsehood.
(ii) The new order presented by the Prophets not only threatens to put an end to their leadership but also would deprive them of the freedom to consume the lawful and commit the unlawful.

For further details, see Surah Al-Anaam, Ayat 103; (Surah Al-Aaraf, Ayats 66-70). 75, 88, 109, 127); (Surah Houd, Ayats 27-28); (Surah Bani-Israil, Ayat 16); (Surah Al-Muaminun, Ayats 24-33, 46); (Surah Saba, Ayat 34 )

sections.title: 26-35 PROPHET IBRAHIM RECOGNIZED THE ONENESS OF ALLAH AND REJECTED SHIRK (POLYTHEISM) AND IF IT WERE NOT THAT ALL MANKIND WILL BECOME ONE RACE OF UNBELIEVERS, ALLAH WOULD HAVE GIVEN THE UNBELIEVER HOUSES MADE WITH STERLING SILVER

translation.text: Call to mind when Abraham said to his father and his people: “I totally disown all whom you serve
I worship only Him who created me, and it is He who will guide me,’

commentary.text: Ibrahim's Declaration of Tawhid Here

For details, see (Surah Al-Baqarah, Ayats 124-133); (Surah Al-Anaam, Ayats 74-84); (Surah Ibrahim, Ayats 35- 41); (Surah Maryam, Ayats 41-50); (Surah Al-Anbiya, Ayats 51-73); (Surah Ash-Shuara, Ayats 69-89), (Surah Al-Ankabut, Ayats 16-27); (Surah As-Saaffat, Ayats 83-100)

translation.text: (Even when they began worshipping others than Allah We did not destroy them) but bestowed sustenance on them and on their forefathers until there came to them the Truth and a Messenger who clearly expounded things to them.

commentary.text: Allah SWT provides for every one of his creations – irrespective of his or her belief in Him.

translation.text: Is it they who distribute your Lord’s mercy? We ˹alone˺ have distributed their ˹very˺ livelihood among them in this worldly life and raised some of them in rank above others so that some may employ others in service. ˹But˺ your Lord’s mercy is far better than whatever ˹wealth˺ they amass.

commentary.text: Allah SWT has no need to justify His decisions to anyone. Allah SWT distributes favors whether it be Prophethood, wealth, privilege/rank etc., to whomsoever He wills.
Wealth or livelihood and rank or status is a favour from Allah SWT -- thus man does not earn these privileges from his own virtue and nor does this mean that Allah SWT loves this person more.
The fact is that Allah SWT has raised some over others so that others are subservient and agree to work for them. Thus, there is a healthy dependency within the community.
But the greatest blessing a mercy from Allah SWT is not wealth or status but Iman and the Quran.

translation.text: Were it not that all mankind would become a single community (and follow the same way), We would have provided for all those who disbelieve in the Merciful One silver roofs for their houses, and (silver) stairs on which to go up,
and (silver) doors to their houses, and couches (of silver) upon which they would recline;

arabic_lines: وَزُخۡرُفًا ؕ وَاِنۡ كُلُّ ذٰ لِكَ لَمَّا مَتَاعُ الۡحَيٰوةِ الدُّنۡيَا ؕ وَالۡاٰخِرَةُ عِنۡدَ رَبِّكَ لِلۡمُتَّقِيۡنَ

translation.text: or that they be made of gold وَزُخْرُفًا.  Surely all this is only the enjoyment of the life of the world. But (true prosperity) in the Hereafter with Your Lord is only for the God-fearing.

commentary.text: (Name of Surah mentioned وَزُخْرُفًا zukhruf-an )
Wealth is not a Sign of Divine Pleasure
The above three Ayat establishes the insignificance or reality of this world

In man's sight the possession of silver and gold is the highest blessing and the very climax of good fortune. Yet, it is so base and contemptible a thing in the sight of Allah SWT that had there been no danger of all human beings being inclined towards disbelief, Allah SWT would have made every disbeliever's house of gold and silver.

The fact is that no matter how much gold and silver one has in this world everything stops at the time of death. We cannot take our homes/wealth with us in our graves. It is nothing but temporary enjoyment of this world. مَتَاعُ الۡحَيٰوةِ الدُّنۡيَا ؕ
True and everlasting prosperity is with Allah SWT in the Hereafter.
This world is meaningless in the sight of Allah SWT which is why He provides for both the believers and the disbeliever’s however the Hereafter is reserved only for the righteous.
Lesson: An abundance of wealth and worldly comforts makes man complacent and forgetful of Allah SWT.
Money, power, status, fame are all tests from Allah SWT so treat them as such.

Hadith: If Allah SWT attributed the importance of worldly wealth equal to that of a mosquito's wing then he would not even give a drop of water to the unbelievers. But for Allah SWT worldly wealth is completely and utterly meaningless – which is why often unbelievers live like kings.

sections.title: 36-45 HE WHO TURNS AWAY FROM THE REMEMBRANCE OF ALLAH, ALLAH APPOINTS A SHAITAN TO BE HIS INTIMATE FRIEND AND HOLD FAST TO AL-QURAN IF YOU WANT TO BE RIGHTLY GUIDED

translation.text: He who is negligent to remember the Merciful One, to him We assign a satan as his boon companion,

commentary.text: Shaytan/satan is the Companion of the One Who turns away from Ar-Rahman
Those who forget to remember and fear Allah SWT (Dhikrir Rahman), and do not give the Quran it's due right, then, for such a person Allah SWT as assigned a satan as his close companion.

translation.text: and these satans hinder them from the Right Path, while he still reckons himself to be rightly-guided.

commentary.text: This satan constantly misguides man, although, ironically man feels he is on the right path. For example, if someone's worldly life i.e job/business are secure and profitable they feel they are successful.

translation.text: But when he comes to Us, he will say (to his satan): “Would that there had been between me and you the distance as between the East and the West. How evil a companion you were!”
(He will then be told): “Today it will not benefit you the least that after your wrong-doing you and your satans now share the chastisement.”

commentary.text: Only in the Hereafter will the person realize what a grave mistake has been made. Of course, that will be of no consequence because retribution will be taken.

Lesson: We must actively strive against satan who comes to us in many forms, including, in the form of humans. At times friends can become our biggest trial who beautiful sins. Satan is working full time to misguide us so we cannot be part time Muslims. A believer’s weapon against satan is the zikr of Allah SWT that includes but not limited to; (i) salah (ii) tasbeeh (iii) and reciting the Quran.

translation.text: So hold fast to what has been revealed to you. Surely you are on the Straight Way.

commentary.text: Encouragement to adhere to the Quran
After the above warning, Allah SWT shows us the way towards salvation –which is the Quran. Hold on tight to the Quran and surely you are on the straight path.
Lesson: Read and understand the Quran as the criteria for success and failure in this world and the next is clearly stated. Do not make man-made criteria's for success or failure as your benchmark.
We must give the Quran its due right, that is, we must (i) recite in Arabic, (ii) understand and (iii) obey.

sections.title: 46-56 PROPHET MUSA WAS SENT TO FIR'ON AND HIS CHIEFS WITH SIGNS BUT THEY RIDICULE HIM AND THE SIGNS AS A RESULT ALLAH DROWNED THEM ALL

translation.text: Indeed We sent Moses with Our Signs to Pharaoh and his nobles. He told them: “I am a Messenger of the Lord of the Universe.”

commentary.text: Musa was sent with the Message of Tawhid to Pharoh and His Chiefs

This story has been narrated here for the Arabs to take heed and learn from the folly of the Pharoh, who on account of his arrogance, pride of kingdom, grandeur and wealth, belittled and mocked the Prophet Musa (PBUH). The unbelieving Quraysh are being warned of a similar fate as the Pharoh.
Lesson: To mock Allah SWT’s revelations and show stubbornness against His warnings is not a mere joke. Take a lesson from the fate of those who have been doomed on account of this.

translation.text: Yet when he brought forth Clear Signs from Us, then lo, they burst into laughter.
Every Sign that We showed them was greater than its predecessor; and then We seized them with Our chastisement so that they may return (to the Right Way).

commentary.text: Allah SWT sent Prophet Musa (PBUH) to the Pharoh and his people to call them towards the exclusive worship Allah SWT. Yet, they remained arrogant and stubbornly refused to obey; in fact rejected and made fun of his message.
The mighty signs Allah SWT sent to Prophet Musa (PBUH):
The miracle of Prophet Musa's hand and staff during the public encounter with the magicians.
For details, see (Surah Al-Aaraf, Ayats 112-126); (Surah TaHa, Ayats 68-73); (Surah Ash Shuara, Ayats 37-51).
A severe famine hit the land of Egypt, as predicted by Prophet Musa (PBUH) and ended only after his prayer to Allah SWT.
Dreadful rain and hail-storms accompanied by lightning and thunder struck the country as per Prophet Musa (PBUH) announcement, destroying crops and dwellings. This was removed only by his prayer.
The sudden appearance of locusts in the land. This calamity also was removed when Prophet Musa (PBUH) prayed to Allah SWT.

Lice and weevils spread throughout the country according to the announcement made by Musa (PBUH), which afflicted men and animals on the one hand, and destroyed barns on the other. This torment was also averted when Prophet Musa (PBUH) was requested to pray for its removal.

Frogs appeared everywhere in the country according to the warning given by Prophet Musa (PBUH), which put the whole population in great distress. This calamity too ended but only after Prophet Musa (PBUH) prayed for it to end.

The torment of blood appeared precisely as foretold by Musa (PBUH), which turned the water of all canals, wells, springs, and pools into blood. Fish died and the water smelled so bad that Prophet Musa (PBUH) was asked to pray for its removal.
For details, see (Surah Al- Aaraf, Ayats 130-136). (Surah An-Naml, Ayat 12) and (E.N. 37 of Surah Al-Mumin).

translation.text: And Pharaoh proclaimed among his people: “My people, do I not have dominion over Egypt, and are these streams not flowing beneath me? Can't you see?
Am I better or this contemptible man who is scarcely able to express himself?

commentary.text: Important to note that Pharon's definition of a despicable person is someone who has no wealth, nor power, nor authority. The disbelieving Quraysh raised this same objection against Prophet Muhammad (PBUH).
Lesson: Align your beliefs and values only and solely with the Quran.

translation.text: And so he fooled his people, and they obeyed him. They were truly a rebellious people.

commentary.text: When a person (ruler) wishes to become autocratic, he contrives every plan openly to achieve his object, he practices every deception and trick. Then, when he has succeeded in his designs and the people (public) have become his obedient servants, they (the public) themselves prove by their conduct and behavior that they are actually what the wicked ruler had taken them to be, and the main cause of their depravity is that they are basically a sinful people. They are not in the least concerned as to what is the truth and what is falsehood, what is justice and what is injustice. Instead, only their personal interests are of real importance to them, for the sake of which they remain ever ready to cooperate with every wicked person, to yield to every tyrant, to accept every falsehood and to suppress every protest that is voiced in favor of the truth.
Lesson: Hence the truth behind the saying, “every nation deserves it’s ruler.”

translation.text: so when they incurred Our wrath, We exacted retribution from them, and drowned them all,
and made them a thing of the past and an example for those who would come after them.

commentary.text: Lesson: One should take a lesson from the stories that Allah SWT has oft repeated in the Quran and not ape the same mistakes. The wise man is one who learns from others.

sections.title: 57-67 PROPHET ISA (JESUS) WAS NO MORE THAN A MORTAL WHOM ALLAH FAVORED AND MADE HIM AND EXAMPLE FOR THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL

translation.text: He was no more than a servant (of Ours), one upon whom We bestowed Our favours and whom We made an example (of Our infinite power) for the Children of Israel.

commentary.text: The Contempt of the Quraysh for the son of Maryam, and His true Status with Allah

Prophet Isa (PBUH) is a man whom Allah SWT bestowed his favor upon and made an example for the children of Israel. “We made him an example,” implies that Prophet Isa (PBUH) was born without a father and granted miracles by Allah SWT that had not been granted to anyone before him nor to anyone after, him, for example, spoke in the cradle, he would make a bird of clay and then breathe life into it; he would give sight to those born blind; he would cure the lepers; so much so that he would raise the dead back to life.

However, it is wrong to worship him as the son of God because of his extraordinary birth and the great miracles granted to him. He was no more than a mere servant, whom Allah SWT has blessed and made an example of His power.

(For details, see (Surah Aal-Imran, Ayats 42-49, 59); (Surah An-Nisa, Ayat 156); (Surah Al- Maidah, Ayats 17,110); (Surah Maryam, Ayats 17-35); (Surah Al-Anbiya, Ayat 91); (Surah Al-Muminun, Ayat 50).

translation.text: Verily he [i.e., Jesus) is a omen of the Hour. So be in no doubt concerning it and follow Me. This is the Straight Way.

commentary.text: One interpretation of this Ayat can be the reference to the second coming of the Prophet Isa (PBUH), that is, when he comes for the second time to the world, then it will become clear that Resurrection is not far behind. However, a more correct interpretation of this Ayat is that the one whose birth was without a father and his raising the dead back to life has been presented as proof of the possibility of Resurrection.

Why do you think it is impossible for God to raise you and all mankind from death when He can create a child without a father and a servant of His can breathe life into an image of clay and raise the dead back to life – but all this only by His permission.

arabic_lines: وَلَا يَصُدَّنَّكُمُ الشَّيۡطٰنُ ۚ اِنَّهٗ لَكُمۡ عَدُوٌّ مُّبِيۡنٌ

translation.text: Let not Satan hinder you (from believing in the Hour), for surely he is your open enemy.

commentary.text: Let not satan, with his constant misguidance, make you so entrenched in worldly affairs that you forget believing in Resurrection.

Lesson: Satan is your OPEN enemy so treat him like you would your worst enemy. Always be on your guard against him as you would be of someone who has declared war against you.  Satan is hell bent on taking us all to Hell.

translation.text: When Jesus came with Clear Signs and said: “I have brought wisdom to you that I may make plain to you some of the things you differ about. So fear Allah and follow me.

commentary.text: The Torah was a Book full of commandments and only commandments (do and dont's). The Bible is a Book full of wisdom. The Quran has both commands and wisdom.

translation.text: Allah is my Lord and your Lord; therefore, serve Him. That is the Straight Way.”

commentary.text: The Prophet Isa (PBUH) himself never claimed that he was God or the son of God, or that people should worship him, on the contrary, his message was the same as all other Prophets, and the same message is now being conveyed to you through Muhammad (PBUH).
For explanation, see (Surah Aal-Imran, Ayats 50-51); (Surah An-Nisa, Ayats 171-172); (Surah Al- Maidah, Ayats 72, 116-117); (Surah Maryam, Ayats 30-36).

translation.text: On that Day even bosom friends shall become enemies to one another, all except the God-fearing.

commentary.text: The Resurrection will come suddenly, and Enmity will arise between close Friends among the Disbelievers

Only those friendships will remain unaffected which are based on righteousness and piety in this world. All other friendships will turn into foes, especially, those who are cooperating with one another in deviation, tyranny and wickedness. On the Day of Resurrection, the blame game will begin and these deviants will want to get as far away from one another as possible.
This subject has been repeated in the Quran numerous times so that every person is fully cognizant as to with whom it is beneficial to cooperate and with whom it is harmful.

sections.title: 68-89 ON THE DAY OF JUDGEMENT BELIEVERS WILL HAVE NO FEAR OR REGRET, THEY WILL BE WARDED PARADISE AND MADE HAPPY AND O PROPHET TELL THE CHRISTIANS, IF ALLAH HAD A SON, I WOULD HAVE BEEN THE FIRST ONE TO WORSHIP HIM

translation.text: (It will be said to them): “My servants, today you have nothing to fear or regret,

commentary.text: May we all hear these beautiful words of: “Enter Paradise joyfully.” اُدۡخُلُوا الۡجَنَّةَ

commentary.text: Good News for Those with Taqwa on the Day of Resurrection, and Their entry into Paradise
Above Ayat’s (43:68 till 43:73) provide a beautiful and descriptive account of how Heaven will look & feel.

translation.text: But the evil-doers shall abide in the torment of Hell
Never will their torment be lightened for them. They shall remain in utter despair.
It is not We Who wronged them; rather, it is they who wronged themselves.
They shall call out: “O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us.” He will reply: “You must stay on in it.
We brought you the Truth; but to the truth most of you were averse.”

commentary.text: The Punishment of the Doomed
A description of the state of the blessed is followed by a description of the state of the doomed. (Above Ayats).

translation.text: If you were to ask them: “Who created them?” they will surely say: “Allah” Whence are they, then, being led astray?

commentary.text: If you ask them who has created them, they will say: "Allah.”

arabic_lines: وَقِيۡلِهٖ يٰرَبِّ اِنَّ هٰٓؤُلَاۤءِ قَوۡمٌ لَّا يُؤۡمِنُوۡنَۘ

translation.text: We call to witness the cry of the Messenger: “O Lord, these are a people not wont to believe!”

commentary.text: Allah SWT is aware when His Messenger says: Ya Rabbi, these are a people who would not believe. They are so utterly deluded that although they themselves admit that Allah SWT alone is their Creator and Creator of their gods, yet, they abandon the Creator and persist in worshiping His creatures.

Lesson: Very sobering reminder for all of us to be aware of who or want steers us away from the 'exclusive' worship of Allah SWT – is it our friends, family, jobs, or our desires? Once we understand then actively strive to distance ourselves from them.

arabic_lines: فَاصۡفَحۡ عَنۡهُمۡ وَقُلۡ سَلٰمٌؕ فَسَوۡفَ يَعۡلَمُوۡنَ

translation.text: Indulge them, (O Prophet), and say to them: “Peace to you.” For soon they shall come to know.

commentary.text: Allah SWT answers, that you should neither curse those who disbelieve for their scornful words and attitude of mockery and derision, nor respond to them with harsh words, rather, instead just wish them well and take your leave.
Lesson: Beautiful lesson for us. Always and in all ways be kind but then actively move away from those who mock or scorn Allah SWT. Very soon the truth will be clear to all.

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: The Surah takes its name from the word dukhan that occurs in Ayat 10.

items.text: فَارۡتَقِبۡ يَوۡمَ تَاۡتِى السَّمَآءُ بِدُخَانٍ مُّبِيۡنٍۙ
(44:10)  (Prophet) So watch for the Day when the sky will come down with a pall of smoke (Duhkan بِدُخَانٍ Smoke

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: This is a Makki Surah and it is fifth in the number of Surahs that begin with HaMim.  It has 59 Ayats in 3 Rukus.

front_matter.label: Subject and Topics
front_matter.text:
There are seven Surahs in the Quran that begin with Ha Mim and they are:  (i) al-Momin (40), (ii) Ha Mim al-Sajdah (41) (iii)Ash-Shura (42) (iv) al-Zukhruf (43) (v) al-Dukhan (44) (vi) al-Jathiyah (45) (vii) al-Ahqaf (46). These seven Surahs are also called "al-Hawamim".  The central theme of all these Surah's is (i) Tawhid (the exclusive worship of Allah SWT) and (ii) Da'wah which means inviting people to the EXCLUSIVE belief/worship in Allah SWT.
The Surah warns about the punishment of Allah SWT which no one can avert it.  The division between the righteous and wicked in the Hereafter will be the final decision of Allah SWT only. A vivid description of Heaven and Hell is provided. This Surah is a pair with the previous Surah Az-Zukhruf and both contain the exact same two beginning Ayats.

sections.title: 1-16 ALLAH REVEALED THIS QURAN IN THE BLESSED NIGHT (LAYLA-TUL-QADR) IN WHICH ALL MATTERS ARE DECIDED WISELY BY HIS COMMAND

arabic_lines: حمٓ.

translation.text: Ha'. Mim.
translation.ref_as_written: as written; context shows 44:1 (source surah-number typo)

arabic_lines: وَالۡكِتٰبِ الۡمُبِيۡنِ

translation.text: By the Clear Book;
translation.ref_as_written: as written; context shows 44:2 (source surah-number typo)

commentary.text: This is not a Book of riddles rather a Book that is clear in its meaning, a Book of guidance that clarifies right from wrong. And a means of establishing a direct link/connection with our Rabb.

translation.text: We revealed it on a Blessed Night, for We were intent on warning;

commentary.text: The night implies the same night that has been called, 'lailat-ul-qadr' in (Surah Al-Qadr, Ayat 1), where it has been said: 'We sent it down in a night of glory', and here it says, 'We sent it down in a blessed night.' Ramadan is the month in which the Quran was revealed,  (Surah Al-Baqarah, Ayat 185).

translation.text: (We revealed it on the Night) wherein every matter is wisely determined

commentary.text: All matters for the coming year are decreed during this night and then the angels carry out Allah SWT's decree. How much provision one will receive, sickness & health, births & deaths, etc. This is the night to make dua as dua can change decrees, therefore, do not take the last 10 nights of Ramadan casually as it can make the coming year a blessed one.
FYI-- This does not happen on the 15th of Shaaban -- as some claim.

translation.text: as a Mercy from your Lord. Surely He is All-Hearing, All-Seeing,

commentary.text: The Quran is described as a Mercy from Allah SWT, so that man is made aware of the distinction between right and wrong, good and evil and thus not left wandering in darkness.
Lesson: One should understand and appreciate the exalted position of the Quran as established by Allah SWT.

translation.text: the Lord of the heavens and the earth and of all that is between them: if you would only have sure faith.

commentary.text: The Arabs themselves admit that Allah SWT alone is the Lord (Master and Provider) of the Universe and of everything in it. Then, it is His right as the Master and our duty as His servants that you should obey every guidance and submit to every command that comes from Him.

translation.text: In fact, they are in doubt, amusing themselves.

commentary.text: Here an important truth has been stated. Even atheists or polytheists find themselves in situations where they’re very being from within affirms and bears testimony that this wise system which extends from the galaxies, to the creation of man, could not come into existence without an All-Wise Designer.

As for the question: Why doesn’t this doubt make them restless and why don’t they seek the truth seriously so as to obtain a satisfactory position for their convictions? The answer is: they lack seriousness in religious matters. What they regard as important are worldly acquisitions and their enjoyment, and this is what they expend all their powers and abilities of the heart and mind and body. Religious matters are viewed as entertainment with endless discussions about denial or negation of Allah SWT's existence.
Doubt results in a lack of seriousness or heedlessness in religion while conviction results in seriousness.

arabic_lines: ارۡتَقِبۡ يَوۡمَ تَاۡتِى السَّمَآءُ بِدُخَانٍ مُّبِيۡنٍۙ

translation.text: (Prophet) So watch for the Day when the sky will come down with a pall of smoke (Duhkan بِدُخَانٍ Smoke

commentary.text: Name of the surah
Prophet (PBUH) is told to wait in anticipation as events turn and the sky will be filled with red smoke --usually a result of drought and famine.
There are two opinions regarding this Ayat:
(i) First is that this smoke refers to the DoJ.

(ii) Second is that Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) prayed to Allah SWT to bring about a famine for the unbelieving mushrikeen. Then Allah SWT revealed this Ayat. The mushrikeen were struck with a severe drought and famine and the land became completely dry with dust/smoke everywhere.

Mostly the second opinion is viewed as correct. The drought and famine are the lesser punishment meant to serve as a warning so that the people of Makkah come out of their heedlessness, repent and change their ways – before the bigger punishment on the DoJ.

translation.text: (People will then say): “Our Lord, remove this scourge from us; we shall believe.”
Yet We will hold the scourge back for a while, (but no sooner than We will do so) you will revert to your old ways.

commentary.text: Allah SWT removed the drought and famine from the people of Makkah upon their request (44:12) but no sooner was this trial removed that the people reverted back to their old ways.
*This Ayat can be the reason why the second opinion in Ayat (44:10) is more acceptable because after the DoJ there will be no relief.

translation.text: The Day when We shall seize them with a mighty seizing, that will be the Day on which We shall inflict upon you full retribution.

commentary.text: Allah SWT says: On the DoJ the unbelievers will not be provided any relief. Maximum and everlasting retribution will take place with no relief in sight.

Lesson: Allah SWT gives us many warnings and signs so we can mend our ways. As literate Muslims it is imperative on us that we acquire knowledge regarding the rights, obligations and duties Islam places upon us because on the DoJ we will not be able to use ignorance or not knowing as an excuse.

sections.title: 17-29 LESSONS TO BE LEARNED FROM THE STORY OF PROPHET MUSA AND THE PEOPLE OF FIR'ON

translation.text: Indeed, before them We tested Pharaoh’s people: a noble messenger came to them

commentary.text: The Story of Musa and Pharon and how the Children of Israel were saved
Before the trial of the famine in Makkha, Allah SWT tested the people of Pharon. Musa (PBUH) was sent to this nation as a Prophet who conveyed the clear message of Allah SWT.

translation.text: [Musa] cried to his Lord, ‘These people are evildoers!’

commentary.text: Despite that numerous miracles and signs Musa (PBUH) showed Pharon and his people they persisted in their disbelief.

Then this was the final verdict that Prophet Muas (PBUH) presented before his Lord, saying: These are the people who are criminals. That is, they’re being the criminals has been confirmed finally and absolutely. They have exhausted every chance of concession and respite for reformation. It is time that the final fatal decision is passed against them.

translation.text: Allah responded, “Leave with My servants at night, for you will surely be pursued.

commentary.text: Allah SWT accepted Prophet Musa (PBUH)'s dua and this was the initial command given for the migration.

translation.text: And leave the sea behind you as calm as ever. Surely they are an army that is doomed to be drowned.”

commentary.text: This command was given when Prophet Musa (PBUH) had crossed the sea along with his caravan and tried to restore the sea to its former state by striking it with his staff so that Pharaoh and his army should not pursue them on the dry path created by the miracle. Allah SWT said: 'Leave the sea divided as it is, so that Pharon and his armies should descend into it. Then the sea will be restored and they will be drowned all together.'

translation.text: How many gardens did they leave behind, and how many fountains
and sown fields and splendid mansions,
and the life of ease in which they took delight!
Thus it was; and We made another people inherit all that.

commentary.text: All the blessings, abundance, and ease were taken away from the people who transgressed all limits. "Another people” here implies the children of Israel, whom Allah SWT made heirs of the land of Egypt after the Pharaoh’s people.
(For a detailed discussion, see (Surah Ash Shuara, Ayats 57-59)

translation.text: Then neither the sky shed tears over them nor the earth. They were granted no respite.

commentary.text: That is, when they were the rulers, they were known for their glory and grandeur and the whole world was devoted to them for their excellences and indebted to them for their favors. But when they fell, there was none to shed a tear, rather the world felt relieved that a cause of distress had been removed. As long as Allah SWT continued to give them respite by His will, they enjoyed life as they pleased; but when they transgressed all limits in their crimes, they were cast aside like rubbish.
Lesson: Pride and arrogance are most often man's greatest downfall. Death is around the corner and we will all soon be part of dirt. We should reflect upon our legacy.

sections.title: 30-42 ALLAH DELIVERED THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL AND CHOSE THEM OVER THE NATIONS OF THE WORLD INSPITE OF THEIR WEAKNESSES AND DAY OF SORTING OUT IS THE TIME APPOINTED FOR RESURRECTION

translation.text: Thus did We deliver the Children of Israel from the humiliating torment,
from Pharaoh . He was truly a tyrant, a transgressor.

commentary.text: There is a subtle satire here for the chiefs of the disbelieving Quraish that, ' you do not enjoy any place of distinction among the transgressors against Allah SWT. Pharon was an arrogant transgressor ruling the largest kingdom of the time as a god. Yet, he was swept away like straw, so how can you prevent the divine wrath'?

translation.text: We knowingly exalted them (i.e., the Children of Israel) above other peoples of the world

commentary.text: That is, Allah SWT had the knowledge of both the good qualities and weaknesses of the Children of Israel. He had not chosen them blindly. He chose them from among the contemporary nations to become the standard bearers of His message and His Tawhid as they were the most suitable people for this purpose.

translation.text: Indeed these people say:

commentary.text: Now the commentary goes back to the Makkans. The people of Makkah say.

translation.text: “This is our first and only death, and we shall never be raised again.

commentary.text: That is, when we die the first time, we shall be annihilated and there will be no other life after that.

translation.text: Bring back to us our fathers if you are truthful.”

commentary.text: If you claim that there will be another life, then resurrect our forefathers from their graves so that we are convinced of life after death. If you do not do this, we will think that your claim is false.

translation.text: It was not in idle sport that We created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them.

commentary.text: Some who don’t believe are very loose and free with their words about Allah SWT and say that maybe there is a god out there but he was bored so he created the world for sport/entertainment.
Allah SWT responds to this idea: This Creation is not a game to Allah SWT.
(This subject will be mentioned again in the next Surah)

translation.text: We did not create them except in Truth. But most of them do not know.

commentary.text: Allah SWT created everything for a reason and purpose, however, most are blissfully unaware. The sun, and moon, night and day are all created for a purpose. Whoever denies life after death and the rewards and punishments of the Hereafter, in fact, regard this world as a plaything. The fact, however, is that this universe is the creation of an All-Wise Creator and thus it cannot be expected from an All-Wise Creator that He would perform a useless and vain act.
For a detailed explanation, see (Surah Al-Anaam, Ayat 73); (Surah Younus, Ayats 5-6); (Surah Al-Anbiya, Ayats 16-18); ( Surah Al-Muminun, Ayat 115); (Surah Ar-Room, Ayats 8-9 )

translation.text: The Day of Final Decision is the appointed time for all;

commentary.text: This is the answer to their (Mushrikeen of Makkah) demand: (44:36) Bring back to us our fathers if you are truthful. They are being told that life-after-death is not a trivial matter, it cannot be that whenever somebody denies, a dead person is raised immediately from the graveyard and presented before him. A time has been ordained when Allah SWT will resurrect to life all the former and the latter generations, gather them together in His court and will decide their cases.

front_matter.label: Subject Matter and Topics
front_matter.text:
The central theme is an invitation to submit to Allah SWT before it is too late. The surah directly addresses the skepticism and objections raised by the disbelievers of Makkah concerning the principles of Tauhid and the reality of the Hereafter. It cautions them about the consequences of their dismissive attitude toward the message of the Quran.
The surah opens by presenting numerous signs across creation that point to the oneness of God. These signs can be witnessed in the human body, as well as throughout the earth and the heavens, inviting people to reflect.
The surah continues by addressing the misconceptions held by the disbelievers regarding the Hereafter. They assert that life consists solely of this world and reject any notion of life after death. In response, the Quran presents several arguments:
Such statements are not based on any real knowledge; rather, they are assertions rooted in mere conjecture and assumption.
Their main rationale is that since they have never witnessed someone rise from the dead and return to this world.
Reason and justice demand that the good and the bad, the obedient and the rebellious, the oppressors and the oppressed, should not ultimately meet the same end. To believe otherwise is a clear misjudgment of the divine order.
The denial of the Hereafter is deeply rooted in the belief by those who wish to follow to their desires, with unrestrained indulgence.

commentary.text: IMAN + GOOD DEEDS = SUCCESS

The discourse, following the invitation to Tauhid, shifts to the essential theme of the Hereafter. Belief in the Hereafter forms the foundation for divine justice which demands that good people are rewarded for their actions, while those who commit evil are punished accordingly. If both groups were to meet an identical end, the very concept of virtue and vice would lose its meaning, and it would amount to an injustice unbefitting the Lord of the worlds.
Those who pursue evil ways often hope for a world without accountability, reward, or punishment, so as to continue with their enjoyment of worldly life.

However, divine wisdom and justice necessitate that God take into account how individuals lived: the believer who maintained moral discipline, fulfilled obligations, refrained from unlawful pleasures, and made sacrifices for the sake of truth should not be equated with the one who indulged every desire, disregarded the rights of God and people, and sought only personal gain.

For further explanation, see: Surah Younus, Ayat 4, Surah Houd, Ayat 106, Surah An-Nahl, Ayats 38-39, Surah Al-Hajj, Ayat 9, Surah An-Naml, Ayat 86, Surah Ar-Rum, Ayats 7-8, Surah Suad, Ayat 28; and 30.

arabic_lines: وَ خَلَقَ اللّٰهُ السَّمٰوٰتِ وَالۡاَرۡضَ بِالۡحَقِّ وَلِتُجۡزٰى كُلُّ نَفۡسٍۢ بِمَا كَسَبَتۡ وَهُمۡ لَا يُظۡلَمُوۡنَ

translation.text: God created the heavens and earth for a true purpose: to reward each soul according to its deeds. They will not be wronged.

commentary.text: Allah SWT did not create the earth and the heavens for mere amusement, but rather as part of a wise and purposeful system. The universe was created in Haq or Truth, and every soul will be recompensed accordingly. It is inconceivable that those who perform good deeds—using the abilities and resources entrusted to them by Allah SWT—should have the same end as those who spread corruption and evil through misuse of those gifts. Without a life after death where deeds are justly rewarded or punished, the universe would appear to be the work of a thoughtless creator, rather than that of a Wise Being.
For further explanation, see references in Surah Al-Anaam (73); Surah Younus (5-6); Surah Ibrahim (19); Surah An-Nahl (3); Surah Al-Ankabut Ayat 75 and Surah Ar-Room Ayat 6.

commentary.text: Now yet another form of arrogance/pride is being mentioned where people live life without fear of any consequences. When someone makes their desires their “god,” it means they let their own wishes and cravings guide them completely. When people are more interested in worshipping their wants or wishes irrespective then Allah SWT, then the consequences of this are mentioned here as well which is the sealing of one’s heart, ears and eyes to the truth.
Sealing the Heart, Ears, and Eyes

When someone keeps turning away from God’s guidance and only follows their own desires, they eventually lose the ability to see, hear, or understand the truth. Their hearts, ears, and eyes become “sealed” against guidance.

This idea is explained in several Ayats, including Surah Al-Baqarah (2:7, 2:18), Surah Al-Anaam (6:25), Surah Al-Aaraf (7:100), Surah At-Taubah (9:87, 9:93), Surah Younus (10:74), Surah Ar-Raad (13:27), Surah Ibrahim (14:4, 14:27), Surah An-Nahl (16:108), Surah Bani-Israil (17:46), Surah Ar-Room (30:59), Surah Fatir (35:8), and Surah Al-Muminun (23:60).

However, the message of revelation has never suggested that individuals will be resurrected on demand during this life. Instead, it teaches that, on the Day of Resurrection, all people will be brought back to life simultaneously for judgment, where each will be held accountable and receive their due rewards or punishment.

front_matter.label: Historical Background
front_matter.text:
The tenth year of the Prophethood was marked by intense persecution for the Holy Prophet, as the Quraish and allied tribes enforced a three-year boycott against the Bani Hashim and Muslims, leaving them besieged and deprived of supplies. Abu Lahab actively encouraged merchants to inflate prices, worsening their hardship.
After the siege ended, both Abu Talib, the Prophet's protective uncle, and Khadijah, his supportive wife, died within weeks, making it a year of sorrow and grief. The Prophet then faced increased hostility in Makkah, including public humiliation. Seeking new opportunities, he traveled on foot to Ta'if to invite its leaders to Islam but was rejected and assaulted. Injured and exhausted, he prayed for strength rather than vengeance.
Returning to Makkah, he worried about further opposition, but found hope when a group of jinn heard him recite the Quran, believed, and began sharing his message.

front_matter.label: Subject Matter and Topics
front_matter.text: Its main purpose is to warn disbelievers about their misconceptions—rejecting accountability, denying the Prophet's mission, dismissing the Quran as God's word, and refusing belief in life after death. It is a pair of the previous Surah. The previous Surah told us to leave arrogance. Here too the contrast between arrogance and humility continues. This is the last of the Ha Mim Surahs.

sections.title: 1-6 ALLAH CREATED THE HEAVENS, EARTH AND ALL THAT LIES BETWEEN THEM TO MANIFEST THE TRUTH AND THOSE DEITIES TO WHOM MUSHRIKIN INVOKE ARE NOT EVEN AWARE THAT THEY ARE BEING INVOKED

arabic_lines: حٰمٓ

translation.text: Ha'. Mim.
The revelation of this Book is from Allah, the Most Mighty, the Most Wise.
We have created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in Truth and for an appointed term. But those who disbelieve have turned away from what they were warned against.

commentary.text: Ayat 1, 2 and 3 are the same as the last Surah. That this is a world with a purpose for a limited period. Warning about the DoJ is given.

translation.text: Who could be more wrong than a person who calls on those other than God, those who will not answer him till the Day of Resurrection, those who are unaware of his prayers,

commentary.text: Shirk is being refuted. No one is more misguided than those who invoke idols (anyone else) besides Allah SWT, asking them for things that they cannot give. They (the idols) are unaware of what he asks, because they can neither hear, see, or act. Like sending an email to the wrong address and expecting a reply.

Usually, this shirk is divided into three categories: 
(1) Lifeless and inanimate creation. 
(2) The pious men who have passed away. 
(3) The wicked men who had themselves gone astray, and who misled others and passed away.

“Those who will not answer him till the Day of Resurrection…” means that during the world or their lifetime they will get no answer to their supplications and prayers from their deities, but when Resurrection will have taken place, the deities will turn hostile to their worshipers themselves, as becomes explicit from the following Ayat.

translation.text: Those who, when all mankind is gathered, will become his enemies and disown his worship?

commentary.text: Shirk is being refuted repeatedly. In this world duas or prayers to false gods will go unanswered and in the other world the false gods will disown them.
FYI – Righteous and pious people would never want to be worshipped. All Prophets including Jesus (PBUH) called people to Tauhid.

sections.title: 7-10 AL-QURAN IS THE WORD OF ALLAH, NOT THE PROPHET AND PROPHET IS BUT A PLAIN WARNER

translation.text: Do they claim that the Messenger himself has fabricated it? (If so), tell them: “If I have fabricated it, then you have no power to protect me from Allah's chastisement. He knows well the idle talk in which you indulge. He suffices as a witness between me and you. He is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.”

Say, ‘Have you thought: what if this Quran really is from God and you reject it? What if one of the Children of Israel testifies to its similarity [to earlier scripture] and believes in it, and yet you are too proud to [do the same]? God certainly does not guide evildoers.’

sections.title: 11-14 AL-QURAN CONFORMS THE REVELATION OF TORAH GIVEN TO PROPHET MUSA

translation.text: Yet the scripture of Moses was revealed before it as a guide and a mercy, and this is a scripture confirming it in the Arabic language to warn those who do evil and bring good news for those who do good.

commentary.text: The Quran confirms the Torah, and the Torah confirms the Quran as divine scriptures.

translation.text: Surely those who say, “Our Lord is Allah,” and then remain steadfast—there will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve.

commentary.text: IMAN + STEADFASTNESS = SUCCESS.
Once you say you believe then remain steadfast on it. Remain firm. For such people Allah SWT promises Paradise.

sections.title: 15-20 THOSE WHO TREAT THEIR PARENTS WITH KINDNESS SHALL BE REWARDED AND THOSE WHO REBUKE THEIR PARENTS SHALL BE PUNISHED

translation.text: We have commanded man to be good to his parents: his mother struggled to carry him and struggled to give birth to him– his bearing and weaning took a full thirty months. When he has grown to manhood and reached the age of forty he [may] say, ‘Lord, help me to be truly

commentary.text: grateful for Your favours to me and to my parents; help me to do good work that pleases You; make my offspring good. I turn to You; I am one of those who devote themselves to You.’
In Ayat 14, after mentioning His Oneness, worship Him with sincerity, and remain upright in obeying Him, Allah follows that by giving instructions regarding the parents.

In this Ayat Allah SWT commands us to be good to one’s parents i.e., both the mother and the father, however the mother’s rights are greater on the grounds that she undergoes greater hardships for the sake of the children.

A Hadith, to the effect that a person asked the Prophet (PBUH): Who has got a greater right to my service? The Prophet replied (PBUH): Your mother. He asked: Who after her? He replied: Your mother. He asked: Who after her? He replied: Your mother. He asked: Who after her? He replied: Your father.

This Hadith precisely explains this Ayat, for here also Allah SWT has mentioned the triple right of the mother: (1) His mother bore him with hardship. (2) She gave him birth with hardship. (3) His bearing and his weaning took thirty months. 

A legal point derived from this Ayat and in Surah Luqman Ayat 14 and Surah Al- Baqarah Ayat 223) which was pointed out by Ali and Ibn Abbas in a law case and made Uthman change his decision.

The story goes that during the caliphate of Uthman, a person married a woman from the Juhainah tribe, and just six months after the marriage she gave birth to a healthy and sound child. The man took the case before Uthman, who declared the woman to be an adulteress and ordered that she be stoned to death. On hearing this Ali immediately came to Uthman and asked: What sort of a decision have you given? He replied: She has given birth to a sound child six months after marriage. Is it not a clear proof of her being an adulteress? Ali did not agree and recited the three above mentioned Ayats in their sequence.

In Surah Al-Baqarah Allah says: The mothers shall suckle their children for two whole years, if the fathers desire the suckling to be completed. In Surah Luqman it is said: And his weaning took two years, and in Surah Al-Ahqaf: his bearing and his weaning took thirty months.

Now, if two years of suckling are taken away from 30 months, six months of bearing remain. This shows that the minimum period of pregnancy in which a sound child can be born is six months. Therefore, the woman who has given birth to a child six months after the marriage cannot be declared an adulteress. On hearing this reasoning of Ali, Uthman admitted that he had not considered that thing at all. Then he recalled the woman and changed his decision.

“And reaches forty years.”., meaning, his complete intellect, understanding, and patience reach the level of maturity. It has also been said that usually one will not change his ways once he reaches the age of forty.

‘Lord, help me to be truly
grateful for Your favours to me and to my parents; help me to do good work that pleases You; make my offspring good. I turn to You; I am one of those who devote themselves to You.’
THIS CONTAINS AN INSTRUCTION FOR ANYONE WHO REACHES FORTY YEARS OF AGE TO RENEW HIS REPENTANCE AND TURN TO ALLAH SWT WITH GRATITUDE.
Our parents blessing has been transferred to us including good family, money, prestige, good education etc. So be grateful to your parents.

translation.text: Such are those from whom We accept their best deeds and whose evil deeds We overlook. They will be among the people of Paradise in consonance with the true promise made to them.

commentary.text: So, making parents happy is making Allah SWT happy.
Hadith: Story about a man who killed a man. To repent he was told to do ahsaan to his parents.
People who are good to their parents then Allah SWT accepts their good deeds in this life.

translation.text: But one who says to his parents, "Uff to you; do you promise me that I will be brought forth [from the earth] when generations before me have already passed on [into oblivion]?" while they call to Allah for help [and to their son], "Woe to you! Believe! Indeed, the promise of Allah is truth." But he says, "This is not but legends of the former people"

commentary.text: Conversely, those who say “Uff” to their parents are being described here. “Uff” literally means the dirt of ear or nails. Something small or dirty that falls on you and you annoyingly blow it away.
There is pride in the child.
Allah SWT has prohibited disrespect towards the parents and especially towards the mother.

translation.text: It is against such that Allah's sentence (of punishment) has become due. They will join the communities of humans and jinn that have preceded them. Verily all of them will court utter loss.
Each ˹of the two groups˺ will be ranked according to what they have done so He may fully reward all. And none will be wronged.

commentary.text: A person will have the rank according to his deeds i.e. not inherited. Compensated fully by Allah SWT. We see the consequences of our deeds in this life as well for example if we are bad to our parents usually our children are bad to us.

translation.text: ˹Watch for˺ the Day ˹when˺ the disbelievers will be exposed to the Fire. ˹They will be told,˺ “You ˹already˺ exhausted your ˹share of˺ pleasures during your worldly life, and ˹fully˺ enjoyed them. So Today you will be rewarded with the torment of disgrace for your arrogance throughout the land with no right, and for your rebelliousness.”

commentary.text: If a person wants the world he will be given (a portion of the world) but then will get nothing in the Hereafter.
The companions of the Prophet (PBUH) feared worldly blessings because they feared they would not get anything in the Hereafter.
Traits Allah SWT does not like and lead to failure. (i) WORLDLY OBSESSION AND (ii) ARROGANCE AND (iii) BEING RUDE OR DISRESPECTING YOUR PARENTS.

sections.title: 21-26 NATION OF A'D REJECTED ALLAH'S MESSAGE, AS A RESULT SHE FACED DESTRUCTION

translation.text: Mention [Hud] of the tribe of _Ad: he warned his people among the sand dunes– other warners have come and gone both before and after him–‘ Worship no one but God: I fear for you, that you will be punished on a terrible Day,’

commentary.text: Allah SWT send Prophet Hud, (PBUH) to the nation of Ad to warn them.  Ad who inhabited Al-Ahqaf.
Ahqaf means a sand dune.  They dwelt among sand (hills) and overlooked the sea. But they rejected! And in their arrogance asked when will the punishment you speak of come?
Name of Surah.
Trait of mocking and denying after knowledge.

translation.text: When they saw a cloud approaching their valley, they said, ‘This cloud will give us rain!’ ‘No indeed! It is what you wanted to hasten: a storm-wind bearing a painful punishment.

commentary.text:
Then, when they saw dense clouds approaching their valleys, meaning, when they saw the punishment coming towards them, they thought the clouds were full of rain. That made them happy and joyful, because they had a drought and needed rain. But infact this was a painful torment!
For eight days and seven nights this violent wind did not stop. Ripping everything out and killing everyone.

sections.title: 27-28 NO DEITY CAN SAVE PEOPLE FROM THE WRATH OF ALLAH

translation.text: Why then did those ˹idols˺ they took as gods—hoping to get closer ˹to Him˺—not come to their aid? Instead, they failed them. That is ˹the result of˺ their lies and their fabrications.

commentary.text: Initially people put faith in those idols/people with the idea that they would attain nearness to Allah SWT through them, but then gradually they made them their gods. They started invoking them for help; believing that they have the powers to change destinies and could answer their prayers and remove their hardships.
Allah SWT sent His revelations through His Messengers over and over again in different ways to bring them to the right path, but they persisted in the worship of their idols/gods.

Now consider this: When the torment of Allah SWT visited these polytheists because of their deviation, where had their redressers of grievances and removers of hardships disappeared? Why didn’t they come to their rescue at the time of affliction?
Thus far we see in this Surah traits of those who are grateful and humble vs those who are arrogant and full of pride.

sections.title: 29-34 A GROUP OF JINNS EMBRACED ISLAM AFTER HEARING AL-QURAN AND BECAME THE PREACHERS TO THEIR FOLK

translation.text: Remember, O Prophet,˺ when We sent a group of jinn your way to listen to the Quran. Then, upon hearing it, they said ˹to one another˺, “Listen quietly!” Then when it was over, they returned to their fellow jinn as warners.

commentary.text: This incident occurred towards the end of the Makkan era with the boycott of Banu Hashim. The year of sorrow because the Prophet (PBUH) lost his wife and uncle. The Prophet (PBUH) had no protection and was chased out of the city but then later went back to Makkah. During the Prophet’s (PBUH) return journey from Taif to Makkah he is feeling very sad. On the way, when he halted at Nakhlah, and the Prophet (PBUH) took comfort by salah and reciting the Quran a group of the jinns happened to pass by and stopped to listen to him. Allah SWT informed the Prophet (PBUH) afterwards by revelation that they had come and listened to the Quranic recitation.
Allah SWT created the circumstances that the two will meet. This happens in life as well. So there is no such thing as coincidence or by chance of meeting someone.
Lesson: Jinn heard accepted immediately and began conveying. Never know who will accept so just give dawa.

translation.text: They said: “Our people, We have heard a Scripture revealed after Moses, verifying the Scriptures revealed before it; it guides to the Truth and to the Straight Way.

commentary.text: This shows that these jinns had already had faith in the Prophet Musa (PBUH) and in the divine Books. After hearing the Quran, they felt that it gave the same teachings as the former Prophets had been preaching. Therefore, they believed in this Book forthwith and in the Prophet (PBUH) who had brought it.

translation.text: Our people, respond to the one who calls you to God. Believe in Him: He will forgive you your sins and protect you from a painful torment.’

sections.title: 35 KEEP ON PASSING THE MESSAGE OF ALLAH AND BEAR THE DISBELIEVERS WITH PATIENCE

arabic_lines: فَٱصْبِرْ   كَمَا   صَبَرَ   أُو۟لُوا۟   ٱلْعَزْمِ   مِنَ   ٱلرُّسُلِ   وَلَا   تَسْتَعْجِل   لَّهُ

translation.text: So bear with patience, (O Prophet), even as the Messengers endowed with firmness of resolve (before you) bore with patience, and do not be hasty in their regard. The Day when they see what they had been warned against they will feel as though they had remained in the world no more than an hour of a day. (The Truth has been conveyed.) Will any, then, suffer perdition except those who disobey?

commentary.text: Allah SWT tells his Prophet (PBUH) that just as the Prophets(Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Jesus) before you went on enduring with patience and steadfast with ceaseless struggle despite the indifference, opposition, resistance and persecutions of their people for years, so you should also do the same, and do not entertain the idea that either the people should believe in you immediately or if they do not believe.
Soon after this the Prophet (PBUH) migrated to Madina.
Meaning of Sabr is to carry on ur work and effort despite all obstacles. Don’t be discouraged. Beautiful lesson for us. فَٱصْبِر
